Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc. We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

About The Team And Role

  • Core Infrastructure builds and operates the foundations of Scribd, Inc.: the paved roads of cloud infrastructure, networking, databases, and observability that let every product team move fast with confidence. Over the past two years, our charter has grown, and today we own the Content Library, the unified storage and governance platform for all content across Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable.
  • The Content Library is one of the more interesting storage problems you'll find anywhere. Nearly twenty years of accumulated content, hundreds of billions of objects in S3, served to hundreds of millions of people every month. It provides transactional storage, dataset transforms with full lineage tracking, low-latency online reads, and the governance layer (access control, trust, deletion propagation) for our most valuable asset: the content that powers our products and our inference-driven features.
  • The core of the platform is written in Rust and built on the excellent Rust data ecosystem (Apache Arrow, Parquet, and DataFusion), with a Python "userland" that teams across the company contribute to directly. If you want a taste of the work, read about Content Crush on our tech blog: https://tech.scribd.com/blog/2026/content-crush.html

job.name: Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer
job.description:
About The Team

At Genesis Molecular AI, we're a tight-knit team of proven deep learning researchers, software engineers, and drug discovery pioneers. Our shared mission is nothing short of revolutionary: to forge the next generation of AI foundation models that unlock new therapies for patients with severe diseases.

We conduct fundamental research at the intersection of machine learning, physics, and computational chemistry, pushing the boundaries of each field.

You will work alongside machine learning researchers, computational scientists, and engineers to build the infrastructure that transforms massive, heterogeneous protein and chemical datasets into reliable, high-performance inputs for our models and drug discovery workflows.

About The Role

We are looking for a Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to build the data and orchestration systems that power molecular AI at Genesis. Drug discovery creates unusual infrastructure challenges: our workflows combine computational chemistry, structural biology, machine learning, and large-scale data processing in ways that don't map neatly onto traditional ETL systems. To meet these requirements, we have built our own pipeline orchestration framework—and we want an engineer excited to push it much further.

This role is deliberately split between building the platform and using it. Roughly 50% of your time will be spent designing and improving our in-house orchestration framework: its DAG abstractions, execution engine, scheduling, caching, observability, and developer experience. The other 50% will be spent building and optimizing the protein, chemical, and ML data preprocessing pipelines that run on top of it. You'll work across both layers, finding opportunities to eliminate unnecessary computation, reduce latency, introduce lazy evaluation and caching, and make complex scientific workflows fast, reproducible, and easy for researchers to use.

job.name: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Backend (Compute Platform)
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Affirm's engineering team is building a large-scale, highly-available, and global infrastructure that is shared across multiple financial products. Ensuring that our infrastructure is accessible to all engineers is critical to the success of the business. We pride ourselves on our culture across engineering of engaging in thorough technical design review, operational excellence, and capable incident response and analysis.

The Compute Platform team owns the EKS foundation that Affirm's products run on, from cluster provisioning and lifecycle through the safety standards that keep thousands of workloads reliable at scale. Affirm operates 90+ EKS clusters across environments and regions, and this team is responsible for making that fleet standardized, automated, observable, and self-healing, while establishing and enforcing the workload configuration standards that protect availability. Our mission is to provide a secure, reliable, and scalable Kubernetes platform that lets infrastructure and application teams deploy and operate with confidence and minimal operational friction.

*What you’ll do* As a Member Of The Compute Platform Organization, You Will Collaborate With Other Teams - Including Product, Infrastructure, Traffic, Cost & Capacity Engineering To

  • Architect and evolve Affirm's EKS platform, driving strategy across cluster lifecycle, node management, and shared cluster components
  • Lead the technical direction for cluster provisioning, upgrades, and teardown through standardized IaC (Terraform, Spacelift) and self-service workflows
  • Own the reliability of core shared components across the fleet (Karpenter, CoreDNS, VPC CNI, Kube Proxy, Metrics Server, etc) and the CI/CD pipeline that ships them consistently
  • Define and enforce EKS workload safety standards covering resource configuration, workload isolation and blast radius, disruption tolerance (PDBs), Karpenter consolidation strategies, etc
  • Build the enforcement and automation path that moves each standard from research and white-glove onboarding through broad adoption to policy-enforced defaults for new workloads
  • Establish the observability, baseline audits, and reporting needed to identify hot spots and measure risk mitigation over time
  • Partner with cluster-user teams (checkout, batch, ML, analytics, DevProd, etc) to understand workload needs and shape the platform accordingly
  • Drive cost and capacity strategy across node scaling, bin packing, and EC2 instance selection
  • Mentor engineers across the Compute Platform teams and set the bar for operational excellence
  • Participate in the on-call rotation, triage and catalogue runtime K8s issues, and collaborate with SRE on production incidents

*What we look for*

job.name: Staff Platform Engineer, Cloud Platform
job.description:
Job Description About the role We want the experience of building and running software on GM's cloud to be as good as or better than what our engineers get from the best developer platforms on their own projects. Pushing code should be quick, getting a namespace or a database should take minutes, and production should stay up without heroics. We are not there yet, and that gap is the job.

This is a Staff-level, hands-on engineering role that spans the whole cloud platform. You will work across GM's internal cloud platform, the foundations underneath it, the control plane that developers interact with, and the runtime that keeps workloads healthy. You will write code, set technical direction, and raise the bar for the engineers around you.

We are hiring a small number of very strong engineers for this. If you have built a scaled platform that people chose to use because it was the easiest path, we want to talk to you.

What You'll Work On You will go where the hardest problems are, and today those include:

  • A platform people choose. Build the default way to ship software at GM so that it is easier than going around it. Move existing workloads onto it without downtime, and keep improving it based on what slows teams down.
  • Self-service infrastructure. Replace hand-built and ticket-driven provisioning with declarative, API-driven infrastructure, covering networking, identity and accounts.
  • Interfaces for people and agents. Design the APIs, CLI and MCP tools that engineers and AI agents use to get work done. Keep them simple and consistent, so no one needs another person in the loop to ship.
  • Reliability at scale. Design for availability and scale, including cell-based and multi-region architecture. Partner with SRE to define SLOs that mean something and remove the failures that page people at night.
  • Fast, safe delivery. Make the path from merge to production quick and boring, with promotion, rollback and policy built in.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build core platform capabilities end to end, from API design through production operations.
  • Set technical direction for one or more platform areas and write the design documents that the rest of the team builds from.
  • Find the biggest sources of developer toil and platform instability, and eliminate them with code and automation rather than process or headcount.
  • Build golden paths so that the right way to ship at GM is also the easiest way.
  • Use AI tooling (Cursor, Claude Code and agents) as a normal part of how you build, and help make the platform itself usable by agents through APIs and MCP.
  • Partner with SRE on reliability, on-call and incident reviews, and hold the platform to measurable SLOs.
  • Mentor senior engineers, review designs and code across teams, and model the engineering standards we want.
  • Work directly with application teams to understand where the platform gets in their way, then fix it.

What We're Looking For

job.name: Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Infrastructure
job.description:
About Us Array Labs is building a new way to understand the physical world.

Today, most geospatial systems are built around flat imagery, incomplete elevation models, slow refresh cycles, or narrow-area surveys. The world increasingly needs something better: accurate, frequently updated 3D information about the places, infrastructure, terrain, and activity that shape human decisions.

Array is building that system. We are developing a coordinated fleet of radar satellites designed to create high-resolution 3D data products of the Earth at unprecedented scale, speed, and reliability. Our technology is built to work across wide areas, through clouds, day and night, and to support both commercial and government customers operating in environments where timely physical-world understanding matters.

We design and build our satellites, radar payloads, sensing systems, and data products end-to-end. Our goal is to make 3D geospatial intelligence dramatically more accessible, useful, and operationally relevant for customers in mapping, infrastructure, disaster response, defense, intelligence, energy, telecommunications, mining, and other industries that depend on understanding the changing Earth.

About The Job As Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Infrastructure, you will own the cloud infrastructure and developer platform that engineers use to build, test, and run everything from radar processing to satellite operations. This includes designing secure and compliant AWS environments, maintaining infrastructure as code, building self-hosted developer tools, and optimizing CI/CD and hardware-in-the-loop testing. You will work closely with software developers, radar engineers, test engineers, and business operations.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate AWS infrastructure (commercial and GovCloud) using Terraform
  • Design and operate our cloud network: VPC, architecture, routing, DNS, VPN, and hybrid links to our ground sites
  • Own cloud security and compliance for a regulated environment: access controls, encryption, audit logging, and continuous monitoring
  • Run self-hosted developer tools, including GitLab, CI runners, observability, and AI infrastructure
  • Build golden path deployment options for internal tooling, and lead the buildout of a developer experience roadmap

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years building and operating production cloud infrastructure as a software engineer or platform engineer
  • Deep AWS experience across multi-account environments, including IAM, VPC networking, and container and compute services
  • Hands-on Terraform experience (or equivalent infrastructure-as-code)
  • Strong networking fundamentals (routing, DNS, VPNs) and the ability to debug connectivity problems end to end
  • Backend software development proficiency: experience building APIs, databases, or other production services
  • Experience building and speeding up CI/CD pipelines and container builds

job.name: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Backend (Compute Platform)
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Affirm's engineering team is building a large-scale, highly-available, and global infrastructure that is shared across multiple financial products. Ensuring that our infrastructure is accessible to all engineers is critical to the success of the business. We pride ourselves on our culture across engineering of engaging in thorough technical design review, operational excellence, and capable incident response and analysis.

The Compute Platform team owns the EKS foundation that Affirm's products run on, from cluster provisioning and lifecycle through the safety standards that keep thousands of workloads reliable at scale. Affirm operates 90+ EKS clusters across environments and regions, and this team is responsible for making that fleet standardized, automated, observable, and self-healing, while establishing and enforcing the workload configuration standards that protect availability. Our mission is to provide a secure, reliable, and scalable Kubernetes platform that lets infrastructure and application teams deploy and operate with confidence and minimal operational friction.

*What you’ll do* As a Member Of The Compute Platform Organization, You Will Collaborate With Other Teams - Including Product, Infrastructure, Traffic, Cost & Capacity Engineering To

  • Architect and evolve Affirm's EKS platform, driving strategy across cluster lifecycle, node management, and shared cluster components
  • Lead the technical direction for cluster provisioning, upgrades, and teardown through standardized IaC (Terraform, Spacelift) and self-service workflows
  • Own the reliability of core shared components across the fleet (Karpenter, CoreDNS, VPC CNI, Kube Proxy, Metrics Server, etc) and the CI/CD pipeline that ships them consistently
  • Define and enforce EKS workload safety standards covering resource configuration, workload isolation and blast radius, disruption tolerance (PDBs), Karpenter consolidation strategies, etc
  • Build the enforcement and automation path that moves each standard from research and white-glove onboarding through broad adoption to policy-enforced defaults for new workloads
  • Establish the observability, baseline audits, and reporting needed to identify hot spots and measure risk mitigation over time
  • Partner with cluster-user teams (checkout, batch, ML, analytics, DevProd, etc) to understand workload needs and shape the platform accordingly
  • Drive cost and capacity strategy across node scaling, bin packing, and EC2 instance selection
  • Mentor engineers across the Compute Platform teams and set the bar for operational excellence
  • Participate in the on-call rotation, triage and catalogue runtime K8s issues, and collaborate with SRE on production incidents

job.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the Team: You will be an integral member of our cross-functional infrastructure team. Working closely with each team of engineers, you will identify the areas that can be enhanced to lower developer’s cognitive load, and make our engineering workflows and pipelines even more efficient. You’ll write common tools, provide development best practices, and guide with thoughtful leadership as we deliver software for our growing customer base world-wide.

  • Embed with teams across firmware, autonomy, cloud, and apps to find workflow bottlenecks and fix them.
  • Measure impact through adoption, cycle time, and quality, and use that data to set priorities.
  • Drive adoption: be the internal expert on AI development tools and help engineers get real value from them.

What Makes You a Good Fit

  • 5+ years building developer tools, infrastructure, or platform systems.

  • Strong grounding in Python/Go/TypeScript/C++, CI/CD, and cloud infrastructure AWS/GCP

job.name: Staff Platform Engineer - Americas
job.description:
We’re looking for a curious, rigorous, problem-hungry platform software engineer (who codes!) to carry the ball as we bring Ashby to the big leagues. Ashby builds software that lets talent teams build an efficient, delightful, respectful hiring process. Similarly, you’re an engineer who wants to build a “paved road” that excellent engineering teams can safely take to the moon and back.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, over 2500 customers, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet, but you now probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role 😅.

About The Role And How We Work Hi 👋 I’m Colin, Head of EMEA Engineering. I’ve spent a number of years leading engineering teams in startups, and that has always included being close to infrastructure teams - no matter what name they’ve worn (SRE, infrastructure, platform, etc). I’ve got my hands dirty building the initial infrastructure for startups and know the value a talented infrastructure engineer brings. The rigour, the discipline, the peace and quiet when everything just hums along .

Our infrastructure is in a good place for now . Nothing is static. Ashby continues to grow rapidly, putting strain on our existing infrastructure. We’re always looking to give our customers more powerful hiring software, and building new product features often requires new pieces of infrastructure.

Having herded plenty of snowflakeservers in the past, I’ve learned there’s a better way. I (and Ashby) place a lot of value on code-as-infrastructure. As a Platform Engineer at Ashby, you’ll get to dive into scaling problems, add new capabilities to our platform, and think about how our entire team interacts with infrastructure. All our own engineers own their projects end-to-end and ship with minimal oversight. We don’t put roadblocks to ensure security when common sense will do and we don’t build processes like change management boards around the lowest common denominator. But with great power comes great responsibility: we handle personal and confidential data about some of the biggest decisions we ever make at work. As we grow, more and bigger customers rely on us to be reliable and secure and how we operate internally will need to evolve.

Read the full description

job.description:
Overview At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of NSD combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Responsibilities Join PNNL’s AI engineering team and help build the next generation of intelligent systems powering national security missions. As a DevOps/Platform Engineer, you'll develop scalable AI platforms, cloud-native infrastructure, and high-performance data pipelines that enable advanced machine learning and real-time intelligence solutions. This role is ideal for early- to mid-career engineers looking to expand their expertise in AI/ML infrastructure, cloud technologies, and distributed systems while working alongside leading researchers and engineers.

What You'll Build

  • Build and deploy cloud-native AI platforms, agentic AI applications, and large language model (LLM) solutions.
  • Develop scalable data pipelines, streaming architectures, APIs, and microservices to process high-volume, real-time data.
  • Design and maintain containerized infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing to support reliable software delivery.
  • Improve system performance, observability, security, and operational reliability across production environments.
  • Collaborate with software engineers, data scientists, and researchers to deliver innovative AI capabilities.
  • Participate in architecture discussions, code reviews, technical planning, and continuous improvement while growing your technical leadership.

job.name: Software Engineer (Kubernetes/Cloud Platform Engineering and Automation)
job.description:
Overview Being good neighbors – helping people, investing in our communities, and making the world a better place – is who we are at State Farm. It is at the core of how we operate and the reason for our success. We're moving with urgency to become a Next Gen Good Neighbor, with technology that strengthens human connections and enhances the customer experience. As an employee, you'll spend less time navigating systems and more time applying judgment, empathy, and expertise in the moments that matter most.

Responsibilities Grow Your Skills, Grow Your Potential Help Engineer the Future of State Farm's Hybrid-Cloud Platform! State Farm is building and evolving a modern enterprise hybrid-cloud platform that supports critical applications across on-premises infrastructure and public cloud environments. We're seeking a hands-on Platform Engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, building automation, and making enterprise systems more reliable, secure, and easier to operate.

In this role, you'll help engineer and automate Red Hat OpenShift Kubernetes Engine (OKE) environments, leveraging Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (ACM) to deliver consistent management and governance across multiple clusters. You'll collaborate with infrastructure, security, application, and cloud engineering teams to support Kubernetes capabilities across on-premises environments and Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA).

What You'll Do:

  • Engineer and Automate: Design, develop, and maintain reusable platform automation using Ansible, Kubernetes/OpenShift APIs, and declarative configuration.
  • Support Platform Modernization: Automate cluster provisioning, configuration, upgrades, patching, certificate management, health checks, and ongoing operations.
  • Drive Consistency and Reliability: Leverage ACM, GitOps, and Argo CD to manage Kubernetes environments, maintain desired state, and improve operational efficiency across multiple clusters.
  • Develop Scalable Solutions: Write scripts, integrations, APIs, and supporting code to eliminate manual processes and create reliable, repeatable automation.
  • Strengthen CI/CD Practices: Integrate automation with GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and code reviews to support safe, consistent platform changes.
  • Champion Security and Stability: Apply secure authentication, secrets management, least-privilege access, and robust error handling to protect enterprise infrastructure.
  • Collaborate and Innovate: Partner across engineering teams to troubleshoot complex challenges, improve platform reliability, share knowledge, and establish effective engineering standards.

You'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on State Farm's growing hybrid-cloud platform while expanding your expertise across software development, infrastructure engineering, and cloud technologies.

Read the full description

With Confluent, organizations can create a central nervous system to innovate and win in a digital-first world.We're looking for self-motivated team members who crave a challenge and feel energized to roll up their sleeves and help realize Confluent's enormous potential. Chart your own path and take healthy risks as we solve big problems together. We value having diverse teams and want you to grow as we grow—whether you're just starting out in your career or managing a large team, you'll be amazed at the magnitude of your impact.

job.description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you.

What You'll Do Platform Infrastructure Engineers (PIEs) are responsible for managing, maintaining, and evolving the foundational infrastructure that supports our internal Infrastructure-as-a-Service platform. PIEs specialize in building robust, scalable, and highly available systems such as Kubernetes clusters, Kafka ecosystems, and cloud environments. They apply sound engineering principles, operational discipline, and mature automation to ensure a reliable infrastructure foundation for all platform services and applications.

Our team helps to improve automation infrastructure reliability. It empowers Braze’s other engineering teams to leverage the infrastructure products and platforms we create easily. Braze operates at a massive scale with over 3.3 billion monthly active users across our customers, collecting hundreds of billions of data points each month and sending billions of messages to end-users daily. We use a diverse technology stack rooted in Ruby on Rails, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, and more. As a Platform Software Engineer at Braze, you will collaborate with your team and consumer engineering teams to build and continuously improve the infrastructure as a service platform that every other team at Braze depends on.

+ Build, optimize, and manage foundational systems such as Kubernetes clusters, Kafka ecosystems, and cloud resources (e.g., EC2, S3)

+ Design scalable architectures to support seamless operations of platform services

job.name: Early Career - Cloud Engineer, Cloud Operations
job.description:
About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary The Cloud Engineer will design, operate, and continuously improve Rivian’s multi-cloud infrastructure with a strategic focus on our expansion into Google Cloud Platform (GCP), AI/LLM enabled workloads, and our already mature AWS environment. This is a hands-on, operations-focused role that drives infrastructure automation, security, observability, and cost optimization for mission-critical cloud workloads.

Responsibilities

  • Leverage AI tools and technologies to deliver cloud solutions that enable teams to operate cloud workloads that are performance and cost optimized.
  • Operate and secure core networking, accounts, and workload identities (IAM/SSO) in GCP .
  • Enable and operationalize cloud services to support AI/ML and LLM workloads, including AWS Bedrock and GCP AI platforms.
  • Automate infrastructure end-to-end using Terraform (IaC), AWX/Ansible, and CI/CD best practices.
  • Maintain and troubleshoot critical workloads, including EKS/Kubernetes environments, HPC clusters, and large-scale storage.
  • Implement and improve observability best practices (e.g. AWS CloudWatch, GCP Monitoring) and participate in on-call rotations and incident response.
  • Drive cost eﬃciency (FinOps mindset) by supporting ongoing cost reviews and optimization efforts.

Qualifications

  • Growth mindset with the ability to evaluate/learn new technologies quickly and apply them to deliver solutions that meet Business needs.
  • Hands-on experience operating production workloads on GCP (AWS is a plus).
  • Expertise in Infrastructure-as-Code (Cloud Formation, CDK, Terraform) and configuration management (Ansible/AWX).
  • Strong knowledge of coreGCP services (GKE, networking, Vertex AI/Gemini).
  • Practical experience with observability tools (e.g., Datadog) and strong debugging skills across distributed systems.
  • Proficiency in a modern programming or scripting language for tooling and automation (e.g., Python, Go).
  • Proficiency in generating software using coding agents; productionizing vibe-coded applications.

Read the full description

job.name: Senior Platform Infrastructure Engineer - USA Remote
job.description:
Bring more to life. At Danaher, our work saves lives. And each of us plays a part. Fueled by our culture of continuous improvement, we turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

Our 60,000+ associates work across the globe at more than 15 unique businesses within life sciences, diagnostics, and biotechnology.

Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference? job.name: Senior Software Engineer, Core Infrastructure
job.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc. We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

About The Team And Role

  • Core Infrastructure builds and operates the foundations of Scribd, Inc.: the paved roads of cloud infrastructure, networking, databases, and observability that let every product team move fast with confidence. Over the past two years, our charter has grown, and today we own the Content Library, the unified storage and governance platform for all content across Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable.
  • The Content Library is one of the more interesting storage problems you'll find anywhere. Nearly twenty years of accumulated content, hundreds of billions of objects in S3, served to hundreds of millions of people every month. It provides transactional storage, dataset transforms with full lineage tracking, low-latency online reads, and the governance layer (access control, trust, deletion propagation) for our most valuable asset: the content that powers our products and our inference-driven features.
  • The core of the platform is written in Rust and built on the excellent Rust data ecosystem (Apache Arrow, Parquet, and DataFusion), with a Python "userland" that teams across the company contribute to directly. If you want a taste of the work, read about Content Crush on our tech blog: https://tech.scribd.com/blog/2026/content-crush.html
  • This role will join an existing team of Senior, Staff, and Principal engineers building the Content Library and Core Infrastructure of Scribd, Inc. for all our production datastores. Working alongside the Content Library's architect and Staff engineers, who set

The team is also responsible for the production environment which requires knowledge with monitoring, alerting and on-call practices. The Platform team performs many functions whether that is tactical operations, providing general solutions for the enterprise or giving guidance or recommendations for individual product teams.

We’re seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Platform Developer II to join our platform team. You will be a force multiplier, enabling our development teams to deliver features faster and more reliably. job.name: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Backend (Compute Platform)
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Affirm's engineering team is building a large-scale, highly-available, and global infrastructure that is shared across multiple financial products. Ensuring that our infrastructure is accessible to all engineers is critical to the success of the business. We pride ourselves on our culture across engineering of engaging in thorough technical design review, operational excellence, and capable incident response and analysis.

The Compute Platform team owns the EKS foundation that Affirm's products run on, from cluster provisioning and lifecycle through the safety standards that keep thousands of workloads reliable at scale. Affirm operates 90+ EKS clusters across environments and regions, and this team is responsible for making that fleet standardized, automated, observable, and self-healing, while establishing and enforcing the workload configuration standards that protect availability. Our mission is to provide a secure, reliable, and scalable Kubernetes platform that lets infrastructure and application teams deploy and operate with confidence and minimal operational friction.

*What you’ll do* As a Member Of The Compute Platform Organization, You Will Collaborate With Other Teams - Including Product, Infrastructure, Traffic, Cost & Capacity Engineering To

  • Architect and evolve Affirm's EKS platform, driving strategy across cluster lifecycle, node management, and shared cluster components
  • Lead the technical direction for cluster provisioning, upgrades, and teardown through standardized IaC (Terraform, Spacelift) and self-service workflows
  • Own the reliability of core shared components across the fleet (Karpenter, CoreDNS, VPC CNI, Kube Proxy, Metrics Server, etc) and the CI/CD pipeline that ships them consistently
  • Define and enforce EKS workload safety standards covering resource configuration, workload isolation and blast radius, disruption tolerance (PDBs), Karpenter consolidation strategies, etc
  • Build the enforcement and automation path that moves each standard from research and white-glove onboarding through broad adoption to policy-enforced defaults for new workloads
  • Establish the observability, baseline audits, and reporting needed to identify hot spots and measure risk mitigation over time
  • Partner with cluster-user teams (checkout, batch, ML, analytics, DevProd, etc) to understand workload needs and shape the platform accordingly
  • Drive cost and capacity strategy across node scaling, bin packing, and EC2 instance selection
  • Mentor engineers across the Compute Platform teams and set the bar for operational excellence
  • Participate in the on-call rotation, triage and catalogue runtime K8s issues, and collaborate with SRE on production incidents

*What we look for*

job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Decisions Orchestration owns key moments in Affirm’s checkout flow, from the screens shoppers see to the behind-the-scenes downstream orchestration and state management that power them.

We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer, Frontend, to set the technical direction for this space. You’ll lead the design of the next generation of Affirm’s checkout experience and raise the bar for frontend engineering across our core checkout flows. Your goal will be to make checkout fast, clear, and reliable.

What You'll Do

  • You will be responsible for setting technical strategy for your team on a year-long time scale, and help your team tie it together with critical, business-impacting projects.
  • You will collaborate across teams in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design & analytics to ensure technical sustainability, risks and trade-offs are well understood and managed.
  • You will act as a force-multiplier for your team through your definition and advocacy of technical solutions and operational processes.
  • You take ownership of your team’s operations and availability by ensuring you have the right monitoring, triage rotations, playbooks, policies, testing and alerting in place to support “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
  • You will foster a culture of quality and ownership on your team by setting code review and design standards for your team, and advocating for them beyond your team through your writing and tech talks.
  • You will help develop talent on your team by providing feedback and guidance, and leading by example.

What We Look For

  • You have 8+ years of experience of developing and architecting web applications using declarative UI frameworks like React or Vue.
  • You are proficient in working with Javascript/Typescript.
  • You have experience delivering major features, system components or deprecating existing functionality in a system through the definition of a technical and execution plan. You write high quality code that is easily understood and used by others.
  • You thrive in ambiguity, and are comfortable moving from low level language idioms all the way to the architecture of large systems to understand how they work.
  • Your growth and impact trajectory demonstrates that you have mastered gathering and iterating on feedback from your engineering and cross-functional peers.
  • You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.

job.name: Sr SIEM Engineer
job.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

  • Job Title & Role Overview

Senior SIEM Engineer — Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Engineering and Detection Content Engineering. Experience required: 4 to 8 years.

Role Overview The Senior SIEM Engineer is a senior technical contributor accountable for SIEM delivery and detection content engineering across the enterprise. You will design, build, test, deploy, tune, and continuously improve detections that draw on SIEM, Network Detection and Response (NDR), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), cloud, identity, network, endpoint, application, and email telemetry.

SIEM Engineering and Delivery

  • Define and maintain the SIEM delivery roadmap in line with Global Security Organization strategy and business priorities.

  • Monitor and improve platform availability, performance, scalability, capacity.
  • Keep SIEM components on supported versions and ensure relevant patches and updates are applied.

  • Maintain engineering standards, technical documentation, architecture artifacts, and operating procedures for the SIEM environment.
  • Identify security-control and detection-coverage gaps and recommend prioritized improvements.
  • Define security key performance indicators and engineering metrics for SIEM and detection capabilities.
  • Maintain documented review of detection exceptions, accepted risks, suppressions, exclusions, and rule changes.
  • Link engineering outcomes to the Global Security Organization’s strategic roadmap and business needs.
  • Qualifications and Experience
  • 4 to 8 years in cybersecurity, security engineering, SIEM engineering, detection engineering, or incident response With a BE/BTech graduation.
  • Strong hands-on experience operating and engineering an enterprise SIEM platform.
  • Experience integrating and analyzing telemetry from network, endpoint, cloud, identity, application, and email platforms.
  • Proven ability to convert threat intelligence, adversary behaviors, and incidents into technical detection content.

  • Data pipeline fundamentals — log ingestion, parsing, normalization, enrichment, schema mapping, correlation, indexing, retention, and data quality.

job.description:

At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

Observability Automation and Service Enablement Engineer About The Role Nationwide's Cyber Security Operations — Innovation and Integration team is hiring a hands-on engineer to operate and continuously improve the observability services behind key systems the team builds and runs. This role blends responsive service delivery with automation engineering: you'll own requests coming through ServiceNow, Microsoft Teams, email, and other channels while evolving the alerting and monitoring around those systems.

You'll manage New Relic alerts and dashboards at scale (1k+) using Python and Terraform, and bring transferable experience with Grafana's LGTM stack — Loki, Grafana, Tempo, and Mimir. This is not a traditional ticket-administration job: success requires a service mindset, sound operational judgment, and the engineering ability to replace repetitive manual work with governed, supportable automation. AI-assisted development experience is a plus — there's room to build agentic workflows that triage and contextualize issues.

What You'll Do

  • Own intake across ServiceNow, Teams, email, and other channels — triage, clarify requirements, set expectations, prioritize, and keep status and fulfillment records accurate.
  • Develop and maintain Python and Terraform automation that generates and deploys New Relic artifacts (dashboards, alert policies, conditions, notification workflows) at scale via APIs, NerdGraph, and NRQL.
  • Partner with application, infrastructure, cloud, security, and platform teams to define useful telemetry, actionable alerts, ownership, routing, severity, and SLIs.
  • Reduce alert noise and configuration drift by tuning thresholds, routing, enrichment, and runbook context, and by reconciling duplicate, stale, or unowned assets.
  • Turn recurring request patterns into governed self-service or automated workflows, and maintain runbooks, standards, and customer-facing guidance.
  • Grow into applying the same engineering patterns to Grafana and the LGTM stack.

job.name: Staff Software Engineer
job.description:
Role Overview

We’re looking for a seasoned Staff Software Engineer who thrives on technical depth and broad influence. You’re as comfortable designing architecture as you are shipping code, and you care deeply about developer experience, scalability, and performance. You’ve likely led modernization efforts, built shared frameworks or design systems, and enjoy helping others adopt better patterns at scale.

As a Staff Software Engineer on our Architecture team, you’ll help shape the foundation of how all our SaaS products are built and experienced. Our goal is to enable product teams to deliver faster, safer, and more consistent customer experiences, and you’ll play an instrumental role in that journey. You’ll collaborate with Senior Engineers, Product Managers, and UX Designers to create a cohesive frontend platform that unites multiple SaaS products into a single, scalable application.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role: Part Architect, Part Builder, and Part Mentor. You’ll lead by example, designing reusable UI frameworks, modernizing legacy codebases, and guiding engineering teams toward better patterns, tooling, and practices. There are no people management requirements for this role.

NOTE: Candidates must reside in Canada.

Why You’ll Love This Role

  • You’ll have outsized impact. The work you do will unlock speed and consistency across multiple SaaS products, laying the groundwork for our next-generation unified platform.
  • You’ll solve meaningful technical challenges. From platform architecture to developer experience, you’ll tackle problems that blend scale, complexity, and usability.
  • You’ll join a culture that values autonomy and trust. We empower experienced engineers to make decisions, move quickly, and see their work make a measurable difference. No ivory towers.

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years of professional software development experience, ideally across both backend (C# or similar) and frontend (React or similar).
  • 5+ years of experience shipping pragmatic SaaS solutions to production (AWS, Azure, or GCP) , balancing technical vision with delivery.
  • Hands‑on experience deploying and operating services in Kubernetes, including containerization, scaling, and troubleshooting.
  • Proficiency with relational and/or distributed data stores (MySQL, Elasticsearch, Redis, Clickhouse, etc.).
  • Excellent mentorship and leadership skills, with the ability to guide and challenge senior developers.
  • Clear and confident communication: you can explain tradeoffs, document patterns, and build trust across Engineering, Product, and UX.
  • Comfortable leading by example: rolling up your sleeves to prototype ideas and prove out new patterns, then scaling those patterns widely through evangelism and mentorship.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a Computer Science related field.

  • Role Type : Full-time
  • Location : Remote

The Role

This is an AI-native fullstack engineering role building micro1's human data platforms. You'll own features end-to-end, from backend services and data pipelines to the frontends our experts use every day.

The role sits between traditional fullstack and research engineering. Coding agents are your primary development workflow, and you'll work closely with research engineers, operations, and product to turn requirements into reliable production systems.

What You'll Own

1. Design and ship fullstack features across backend APIs, data pipelines, and React frontends.

2. Own client-facing data delivery and platform infrastructure, including exports, access control, and reliability.

3. Scope work around outcomes, direct coding agents—often in parallel—review changes at the architecture level, and iterate until shipped.

4. Build and maintain services in Python (FastAPI) and TypeScript.

5. Contribute to data modeling, schema design, and query performance across relational and document databases.

6. Partner with research engineering, operations, and product to translate platform needs into production-ready systems.

7. Improve the frameworks, checks, and evals that make agent-driven development faster without sacrificing quality.

8. Troubleshoot production issues and build resilient, observable systems.

What We're Looking For

1. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

2. 0–5 years of software engineering experience, or strong shipped projects as a recent graduate.

3. Strong fundamentals in Python and TypeScript, with experience building CRUD applications using frameworks such as FastAPI/Flask and React.

4. Working knowledge of databases such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or SQLite and core data modeling principles.

5. Experience deploying services on a major cloud platform (GCP, AWS, or Azure).

6. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex are your default development workflow, and you can clearly explain how you use them.

7. Ability to turn outcomes into plans, direct agents, verify results, and identify architectural issues agents may miss.

8. Understanding of agent loops, MCP, tool/data integrations, permissions, and security.

9. Familiarity with context management, RAG, and evals for testing agent workflows.

Preferred

1. Exposure to RL concepts or environments, including tasks, actions, and rewards.

2. Experience with coding data pipelines or task-authoring platforms.

3. Familiarity with CI/CD, deployment pipelines, and DevOps fundamentals.

4. Experience contributing to team projects, open-source software, or startups.

job.name: Senior Mobile Engineer (Remote)
job.description:
• Role Title : Senior Mobile Engineer (Remote)
  • Role Type : Contractor (~15 hrs a week)
  • Location : Remote

In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input.

As an expert, you will create Reinforcement Learning Environments that test an AI model’s ability to solve complex mobile software engineering problems related to fixing code, creating features, refactoring code, and optimizing performance. You will be tasked with creating a reproducible environment and a golden reference solution for each problem.

Scope of Work

1. Create realistic, interesting, and extremely challenging mobile coding tasks for frontier AI models using your preferred repositories.

2. Design problems that require strong mobile engineering skills, such as tracking down subtle bugs, building non-trivial features, handling application state and lifecycle, or improving performance.

3. Develop tasks relevant to your expertise: cross-platform applications using TypeScript, JavaScript, or Dart; iOS applications using Swift; or Android applications using Kotlin.

4. For each task, define the problem, build a reproducible environment, and write deterministic verifiers that accept correct solutions across different valid implementations while rejecting incorrect, incomplete, or hard-coded approaches.

5. Provide a reference solution showing how the task can be solved.

Preferred Qualifications

1. Significant hands-on expertise in at least one of the following mobile development tracks:

2. Cross-platform: TypeScript or JavaScript with React Native, or Dart with Flutter.

3. iOS: Swift with SwiftUI or UIKit.

4. Android: Kotlin with Jetpack Compose or the Android View system.

5. Deep understanding of mobile application architecture, state management, asynchronous programming, and application lifecycle.

6. Proven ability to debug complex mobile applications, resolve bugs, and deliver effective performance improvements.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete work may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow. Minimum weekly submission requirements apply and will be communicated during onboarding.

Start Timeline & Availability

1. We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

What You’ll Do

1. Create realistic, interesting, and extremely challenging mobile coding tasks for frontier AI models using your preferred repositories.

2. Design problems that require strong mobile engineering skills, such as tracking down subtle bugs, building non-trivial features, handling application state and lifecycle, or improving performance.

job.name: Cybersecurity Expert – Energy Sector (OT/ICS security advisor)
job.description:
Hiring for GOPA Consulting Group — via Flexiple, the recruiting partner on this role.

About the Company

GOPA Tech is the engineering arm of the GOPA group, a German consulting firm with 60 years of work on public-sector and development projects. Its engineers and consultants advise power utilities, governments and international funders such as the EU, World Bank, KfW and EBRD across energy, transport, water and urban development. The Power Systems team covers generation, transmission lines, grids and substations through studies, design, supervision and advice, including SCADA, smart grids and cyber security. GOPA Tech is adding an OT cybersecurity expert to its energy advisory projects.

About the Role

This is a freelance / contract advisory role working from GOPA Tech's office in Baner, Pune. You won't run one company's security operations day to day. You'll go into power utilities, assess how exposed their operational technology (SCADA, ICS, substations) and business systems are to cyber threats, recommend fixes, help plan their digital upgrades and train their staff. The projects are typically funded by international development banks and the EU, with clients in Europe and its neighbourhood.

What you'll do

  • Assess power utilities' cybersecurity against the EU NIS2 Directive and IEC 62443, and write up gaps, risks and priorities
  • Review OT environments (SCADA, EMS/DMS, substation automation, ICS networks) and recommend segmentation, controls and security roadmaps
  • Assess the digitalisation level of energy utilities and help shape digitalisation strategies
  • Advise on OT modernisation and on business platforms such as ERP, billing, CRM and MIS/BI reporting, including integrations, data flows and requirements specifications
  • Run training, workshops and knowledge transfer for utility staff
  • Work alongside GOPA's power systems engineers and the client's project teams, on site where needed

What you bring

  • 5+ years in ICT, digital transformation or cybersecurity in the energy sector
  • Hands-on OT / ICS / SCADA cybersecurity work for power utilities, grid operators or power plants, including IEC 62443
  • Experience assessing organisations against the NIS2 Directive (gap analysis, readiness or compliance assessment)
  • A professional security certification such as GICSP, CISSP or an ISA/IEC 62443 certificate
  • Consulting or advisory delivery: assessments, audits, strategies or roadmaps you have written for a client
  • A degree in IT, Computer Science, Information Systems, Electrical Engineering, Cybersecurity or a related field
  • Fluent English, written and spoken

Nice to have

job.name: Senior Compliance Research Analyst
job.description:

We are looking for a technically strong and detail-oriented Senior Compliance Research Analyst with 5–8 years of experience to join our Security Compliance and Research team. The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on expertise in Linux system administration and security hardening, compliance frameworks, technical control research, and automation using Python, Shell scripting, and PowerShell.

This role involves independently researching, analyzing, developing, validating, and maintaining technical compliance policies and configuration standards based on industry benchmarks such as CIS Benchmarks and DISA STIGs. The candidate will translate security requirements into actionable technical controls, develop automated compliance checks, map controls to industry frameworks, and maintain high standards of technical accuracy and content quality across supported technologies.

The ideal candidate should combine a strong understanding of operating systems and security configurations with a practical approach to scripting, automation, and AI-assisted tooling. The role requires ownership of assigned research and content development activities, independent problem-solving, and effective collaboration with cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Technical Research and Compliance Policy Development
  • Independently research, analyze, and interpret security benchmarks, technical standards, and compliance requirements, with a primary focus on Linux operating systems, followed by other operating systems, applications, databases, and network security devices.
  • Translate security requirements into implementable technical controls, including configuration parameters, validation logic, expected values, remediation procedures, and supporting documentation.
  • Analyze control intent, technical feasibility, security impact, and applicability across different technologies and platform versions.
  • Map technical controls to security and compliance frameworks such as NIST SP 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, and MITRE ATT&CK, where applicable.
  • Take ownership of assigned compliance content throughout its lifecycle, ensuring consistency, traceability, and timely delivery.
  • Linux Systems Security and Hardening

By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. job.description:
About The Role At Abnormal AI, we are on a thrilling mission to safeguard the world's largest enterprises against a vast range of relentless email and collaboration application cyber security attacks. Our relentless pursuit involves crafting an exceptional suite of products that empowers customers to seamlessly visualize, expertly control, and fearlessly combat cyber-security threats.

The Multi-Product Platform (MPP) organization owns the product platform that enables scalable product development, helping the business build and launch enterprise-grade products with a consistent customer experience.

This is a chance to build the data backbone that every Abnormal product depends on. As a Senior Software Engineer on MPP and founding engineer of the team, you'll create the standardised data layer that becomes our single source of truth — the one governed path through which any system, agent, or interface can reach data from across every product, from a single record to cross-product aggregates, online or offline, in whatever shape it needs. A hard, high-leverage problem: serve the whole platform at high throughput and low latency without becoming the bottleneck, while enforcing tenant isolation, auth, and fine-grained access control so every team gets security and reliability for free — built AI-native from day one.

You won't be maintaining someone else's system — you'll be defining the foundation every product is built on, where getting it right compounds across the whole company.

If you're energized by 0→1 platform work, driving cross-team standards, and owning a system end-to-end, this role is built for you.

What You'll Do Technical Delivery & Operational Excellence

  • Design, build, and iterate on the APIs and services that make up the standardized data access layer.
  • Drive adoption of API-gated data sources, so product teams expose their data once and every consuming surface can reuse it, instead of building one-off integrations.
  • Design and implement standard labeling for data ownership, and build the validation logic that checks incoming requests against it.
  • Own reliability, latency, and operational excellence for a high-throughput, low-latency system on the critical request path.
  • Make the early architectural calls and codify them in technical design docs the team aligns on.
  • Establish the team's engineering practices — testing, code/design review, on-call, and CI guardrails — and the patterns future hires inherit.

The Mission Kong Cloud Gateways is Kong's foundational cloud-native SaaS platform, powering its managed API and AI Gateway offerings. It provides a multi-tenant control plane, automation, and platform services that enable customers to securely deploy, operate, and scale dedicated gateway infrastructure with the simplicity of a fully managed cloud service.

At its core, building and operating this platform is a large-scale software engineering challenge, involving complex distributed systems, automation, and infrastructure orchestration. The platform must deliver 4-9s (99.99%+) reliability while operating across multiple clouds, regions, and highly distributed customer environments. Achieving this requires deep software engineering expertise and strong distributed systems fundamentals, with a focus on scalability, resilience, performance, and multi-tenancy.

As an engineering Manager for Managed Gateways Platform, you will take full ownership of the engineering charter, leading and growing the team while being accountable for the architecture, development, delivery, and operation of this multi-tenant SaaS platform. With Cloud Gateways growing 100% YoY and becoming increasingly central to Kong's API and AI strategy, your work will directly influence product innovation, customer experience, platform economics, and our ability to serve some of the world's largest enterprises at global scale.

This is a highly technical Software Engineering leadership role building the software platform behind a globally distributed, multi-cloud SaaS infrastructure product, with end-to-end ownership of everything from code to production infrastructure. It sits at the intersection of hardcore software engineering, distributed systems, and large-scale infrastructure ownership. We believe in a you-build-it-you-run-it model, where engineering teams take 100% ownership of the systems they build, from architecture and implementation through deployment, reliability, and production operations . Founded by economist and AI strategist Dr. Matt Hasan, AIHM unites researchers, business leaders, policymakers, educators, and community members around the question of how humanity can grow intellectually and socially alongside AI. The organization’s core frameworks—Human-AI Cognitive Co-evolution (HACC) and Human-AI Cognitive Outsourcing (HACO)—explore both the benefits of meaningful human-AI collaboration and the risks of over-delegating intellectual responsibility to machines. AIHM advances original research, informs public discourse, influences policy, and supports institutions in adopting AI in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, human capabilities. The movement is pro-human, committed to shaping a future where humans and AI evolve together for greater prosperity and expanded human potential.

The specialist will collaborate with researchers, content creators, and leadership to translate complex ideas into clear, engaging web experiences, while maintaining site performance, security, and scalability. Daily tasks involve coding and testing features, updating layouts and content, integrating third-party tools, monitoring analytics, and troubleshooting technical issues. The role also requires contributing to the overall web strategy, proposing improvements, and aligning all web development efforts with AIHM’s mission and branding.

job.name: Forward Deployed Engineer (Python + AI) - Remote - USA
job.description:
About FullStack FullStack is your AI-native engineering partner, built to turn AI capability into certainty. Most companies can demo AI; few can get it to production and prove what it produced. We close that gap with three capabilities, AI built into your products from the start, elite vetted talent who apply it, and transparent execution that shows value every step of the way. With now over 600 customers in North America, FullStack is one integrated partner for all your AI engineering needs. With FullStack, you move forward with confidence.

We’re Most Proud Of

  • Offering life-changing career opportunities to talented software professionals across the Americas.
  • Building highly-skilled software development teams for hundreds of the world’s greatest companies.
  • Having delivered hundreds of successful custom software solutions, which have positively impacted the lives and careers of millions of users.
  • Our 4.1-star rating on GlassDoor.
  • Our client Net Promoter Score of 68, twice the industry average.

The Position Forward Deployed Engineers sit inside the client’s problem, not next to it. You embed with an enterprise team, find the work that actually warrants AI, architect the system, build it, and stay long enough to make it survive contact with production.

This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer. You should be as comfortable pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering as you are diagnosing why retrieval quality collapsed after a data refresh. The people who succeed here can hold a discovery conversation on Monday and ship what they scoped on Thursday.

On this track, your edge is data, retrieval, and model behavior: you make agents trustworthy by getting the data, context, and evaluation right.

We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up.

How We Approach The Work FDEs are trusted to shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for architect-level judgment:

  • Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec.
  • Decomposes the problem. Outcome → process → decisions → data → systems → actors → constraints — before choosing technology.
  • Chooses the intervention. Remove, simplify, traditional software, automation, LLM, RAG, agent, or multi-agent — and defends why.
  • Owns the architecture decision. Documents trade-offs (ADRs), sets success metrics, pushes back on scope that won’t deliver value.

Consultative Discovery Clients rarely arrive with a fully formed problem, and the FDE’s first contribution is helping them see it clearly. You lead discovery with genuine curiosity, moving the conversation from stated requirements to underlying needs, and you build credibility through the depth of your understanding rather than the breadth of your pitch.

job.name: Software Engineer, Agent Delivery

About Pallet Pallet is building AI Agents to transform the physical economy, a $12 trillion global TAM. We've raised $50M from top investors, including General Catalyst, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures.

Our mission is to increase the efficiency of the global supply chain by automating the manual workflows that slow supply chain teams down. Our flagship platform provides end-to-end visibility, and control.

As companies across the physical economy look to drive efficiency, many are turning to Pallet to lead the way. With deep supply chain expertise and cutting-edge AI capabilities, we're positioned to build the next $10B company powering the physical economy.

Join us and work alongside leaders from Google, DoorDash, YC, and more to shape the future of supply chain technology.

About The Role We're hiring a Software Engineer, Agent Delivery to deploy production AI agents inside some of the world's largest supply chain companies.

You'll work directly with customer operators, engineers, and executives to understand how critical workflows actually run. Then you'll design integrations, debug production systems, and ship AI-powered workflows into environments that are often undocumented, fragmented, and business-critical.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, product, and customer operations. You'll own deployments from initial discovery through production launch, spending time with customers both remotely and onsite, solving complex operational problems and turning those solutions into reusable product capabilities.

Success in this role is measured by outcomes: can you get systems live, make them reliable, and solve problems in environments you don't fully control? Every deployment teaches us something new about how supply chain companies operate. The patterns you uncover become product features, and what you solve for one customer often becomes a capability we ship across the platform.

job.name: Software Engineer, Product
job.description:
About David AI At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

About Our Product Engineering Team The winning voice models will be built on the best systems for collecting human speech data and evaluating their models. Our challenge as engineers is to measurably improve our customers' models by building the most scalable and effective platforms for collecting speech data, verifying and refining its acoustic quality, and evaluating models.

You would build products with real users:

  • Tens of thousands of users take on work in our data collection platform and get paid for recording and transcribing audio, reviewing model outputs, and more.
  • Slingshot is where our operators run the business and decide what ships.
  • Data Marketplace is where customers search for and download research-grade datasets, and run and interact with private evaluations of pre-release models.

Every data product we sell runs through these surfaces: conversation data for speech-to-speech models, emotive speech for TTS, transcriptions for ASR, evaluations of public and private models, and more.

About This Role Product quality shows up directly in our outputs. A confusing Babel flow produces bad recordings. A Slingshot view that buries a problem lets operators ship it to a customer. You will own features end to end, from the interface a contributor or operator sees to the service and pipeline behind it, and you will ship to production daily.

As a Product Engineer at David AI, you will work closely with researchers, both in house and the labs'. We work with them to understand what to measure and which data to collect next, and we turn that into products that run at scale. When our researchers finds a new kind of data that could improve models, you build the recording flows and quality checks that turn it into something we can sell. Our ML team builds models that run inside these products, and you help take them to production.

We’re hiring product engineers across the stack and at varying levels of experience, and will place you on the team where your strengths fit best, whether that leans toward interfaces, backend systems or both.

job.name: Founding Engineer
job.description:
A high-growth AI-native startup is hiring a Founding Engineer in San Francisco to join the earliest engineering hires and shape the architecture, culture and standards of what comes next.

This is a proper founding role. You’ll ship production code from day one, make the foundational architectural calls, sit alongside the founders on every product decision and set the bar as the team scales behind you. Wide scope, no hand-holding, and ownership that only exists at this stage.

Role: Founding Engineer

Salary: $180,000 - $300,000 plus equity

Location: San Francisco, 5 days per week in office

What you’ll be doing:

  • Build core product features end to end across Python, TypeScript, React and Next.js
  • Make foundational architecture, tooling and infrastructure decisions that will carry the product for years
  • Ship fast, iterate on real user feedback and hold a high bar for what goes to production
  • Work directly with the founders on product direction, prioritisation and technical trade-offs
  • Own reliability, performance and cost from the start, not as later problems
  • Shape hiring, engineering culture and standards as the team grows behind you
  • Use AI tooling (Claude, Cursor and similar) across every part of your workflow

What you’ll need:

  • Strong commercial engineering experience, ideally as an early hire at a fast-growing startup
  • Strong Python, TypeScript, React and Next.js in production
  • Track record of shipping product end to end, not just contributing to someone else’s codebase
  • Comfortable making architectural calls with incomplete information and revisiting them when needed
  • Fluent in modern AI engineering tools and able to use them to materially raise your output
  • Happy working 5 days a week in-person with a small, high-intensity team

Nice to have:

  • Prior Founding Engineer experience at a YC or similarly fast-growing startup
  • Exposure to AI/LLM product work, agents or ML infrastructure
  • A shipped side project you can talk about with real pride

This role would suit an engineer who wants to skip the layers, build alongside founders and put their name on the earliest bricks of something ambitious.

At Meta, we are shaping innovative experiences in service of giving people the power to build community and bring the world closer together. job.name: Staff Software Engineer, Frontend (Decisions Orchestration)
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Decisions Orchestration owns key moments in Affirm’s checkout flow, from the screens shoppers see to the behind-the-scenes downstream orchestration and state management that power them.

We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer, Frontend, to set the technical direction for this space. You’ll lead the design of the next generation of Affirm’s checkout experience and raise the bar for frontend engineering across our core checkout flows. Your goal will be to make checkout fast, clear, and reliable.

What You'll Do

  • You will be responsible for setting technical strategy for your team on a year-long time scale, and help your team tie it together with critical, business-impacting projects.
  • You will collaborate across teams in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design & analytics to ensure technical sustainability, risks and trade-offs are well understood and managed.
  • You will act as a force-multiplier for your team through your definition and advocacy of technical solutions and operational processes.
  • You take ownership of your team’s operations and availability by ensuring you have the right monitoring, triage rotations, playbooks, policies, testing and alerting in place to support “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
  • You will foster a culture of quality and ownership on your team by setting code review and design standards for your team, and advocating for them beyond your team through your writing and tech talks.
  • You will help develop talent on your team by providing feedback and guidance, and leading by example.

What We Look For

  • You have 8+ years of experience of developing and architecting web applications using declarative UI frameworks like React or Vue.
  • You are proficient in working with Javascript/Typescript.
  • You have experience delivering major features, system components or deprecating existing functionality in a system through the definition of a technical and execution plan. You write high quality code that is easily understood and used by others.
  • You thrive in ambiguity, and are comfortable moving from low level language idioms all the way to the architecture of large systems to understand how they work.
  • Your growth and impact trajectory demonstrates that you have mastered gathering and iterating on feedback from your engineering and cross-functional peers.
  • You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.
  • This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

Base Pay Grade - P

Equity Grade - USA 13
