job.name: Android Developer
job.description:
Android Architect

Big things are happening in Sunnyvale! 🚀

Oloid has just opened a brand new US tech hub, and we're building the team that will power round-the-clock support for our customers. Engineers, product people and customer champions, all working side by side to make frontline access fast, secure and effortless.

We're growing quickly, the roadmap is ambitious, and the people who join now will shape what Oloid becomes next.

Next up: an Android Architect to design and build our Android software. Could that be you?

THE ROLE

You'd be one of the founding hires of the Sunnyvale hub, reporting into our core executive team. It's a lean team, so you own a workflow end to end and have real influence over your scope of work, how the team is built and who joins next. Frontline teams increasingly work on managed, shared and rugged Android devices, and every one has to know who is holding it, clean up after the last person and behave under kiosk policy. We want an Android Architect who designs it and builds it.

WHY NOW

  • 2027 is a big year for us: revenue is up 600 percent since our Series A and we're going after seven figure enterprise deals
  • Microsoft retires SMS and voice MFA in Entra ID in February 2027, which pushes every enterprise toward exactly what we build
  • Healthcare is our next big market, and Aura, our AI identity assurance agent, is already part of Workday's Agent System of Record
  • The Sunnyvale hub is where that next chapter gets built, and the people who join now are the ones who shape it

IS THIS YOU?

Be honest with yourself on this one: it's not for the faint hearted. You'll wear many hats, move between building, fixing and talking to customers, and make calls without a playbook to lean on. If you've worked in a high growth environment and bring a growth mindset, you'll thrive here.

WHY OLOID

Oloid builds passwordless identity for the 1.8 billion people who work on the frontline: the nurse, the line worker, the store associate who moves between shared workstations all shift, often with no work smartphone. They sign in with a face, a badge tap or NFC, on Windows, Linux and Android, layered onto Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Identity and the systems a company already runs. Tyson Foods, PepsiCo, GE, Takeda, Flex and Honeywell are customers, and we're backed by Dell Technologies Capital, Okta Ventures and Honeywell Ventures.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Own the architecture and production Kotlin and Java for our Android software
  • Design shared device sign in, sign out, session cleanup, offline behaviour and recovery
  • Integrate Android Enterprise, managed configurations, EMM and UEM policies and OEM SDKs • Diagnose device, OS, policy and network failures with evidence, and lead customer technical conversations

WHAT YOU BRING

The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Job Summary: This job implements tasks within the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), follows internal conventions and procedures, makes technical decisions, collaborates with peers and project leads, and contributes to code and design reviews. Our platform integrates implantable neural interfaces, adaptive algorithms, and assistive devices to translate neural intent into real-world action. Our initial focus is stroke-related motor impairment, with planned expansion into cognitive decline and other neurological disorders.

The Role We're looking for a Staff Mobile Software Engineer who is passionate about building beautiful, intuitive mobile applications. Technical Leadership & Regulated Delivery

job.name: Senior Android Engineer
job.description:
About Medium Medium is one of the world's most influential writing platforms, connecting millions of readers with ideas that matter. We're a small, dedicated team that cares deeply and takes real ownership of the problems we tackle, moving fast while building something that lasts. Our actions and decision-making are guided by four principles: Humans First, Deepen Understanding, Orient for Impact, and Ladder Together.

About The Role We're looking for a Senior Mobile Engineer to help build and evolve the Android experience that millions of readers and writers rely on every day. You'll own Android features end to end. That means digging into what users actually need, building it, shipping it, and paying attention to how it actually performs once it's out in the world. You'll work closely with our design team the whole way through.

This is a product engineering role at heart. We don't have a dedicated product team, so you won't be handed a fully-specified ticket and told to go build it. Rather, you'll be the one figuring out what's worth building in the first place, partnering with design and other engineers, and making good calls when the ask is vague or doesn't quite solve the real problem. Android is where you'll spend most of your time, but we want someone who can also hold their own on at least one other platform, whether that's web, iOS, or backend. That range matters: it means you can see how a feature fits into the bigger picture, make good calls about where logic should live, and work credibly with whoever owns that other platform.

What You'll Do

  • Own Android features end to end. Understand the problem, build it, ship it, and see how it actually does
  • Shape what gets built, not just how it gets built. Push back on scope, propose simpler solutions, and raise platform constraints early rather than after the fact
  • Write idiomatic, well-tested Kotlin and Compose UI that fits naturally into the team's existing architecture
  • Work directly with iOS, web, or backend engineers depending on what a feature needs, and help decide where functionality should live
  • Partner with our leadership team, design team, and engineers in the US and France to turn a rough idea into something that actually ships well on Android
  • Bring superb judgment to ambiguous requests. You can ask good questions, spot edge cases early, and propose reasonable first steps when the full scope isn't clear yet
  • Own shaping product and feature spaces, maintaining and driving a sense of forward momentum even when the final destination of your work may not be clear
  • Help raise the bar for the mobile team on code quality, testing, and product thinking
  • Attend Medium's twice-yearly, in-person offsites (hosted in locations around the U.S.)

What You Have

Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. job.description:
Description Shape the future of AI infrastructure! Join AWS as we scale our Manufacturing Test Engineering team developing comprehensive testing solutions for our innovative AI acceleration hardware, deployed across our global server fleet. Annapurna Labs (our organization within AWS) designs hardware and software that accelerates innovation. Our custom chips, accelerators, and software stacks enable breakthrough performance in cloud computing, helping customers solve previously impossible challenges.

We're expanding our AI Hardware Test Organization and seeking a Manufacturing Test Engineer to develop, deploy and sustain the tests that qualify the boards, sleds and systems inside our machine learning training systems. In this role you will own test development for assigned products and test insertions — writing test plans, building automated test suites, validating them against known-good and known-bad units, and deploying them to our manufacturing partners. You will work alongside hardware designers, software engineers, and manufacturing operations throughout the product development cycle, and you will own your tests once they are running on the line: triaging failures, closing coverage gaps, and keeping stations healthy at multiple sites.

Our training systems are built from several kinds of hardware — accelerator baseboards, switching and interconnect sleds, trays, and complete racks — and your assignment will follow the program's needs rather than a single fixed product. What stays constant is the work itself: taking a new or changed design through test development, proving the test catches real defects, and keeping it healthy once a factory is running it at volume.

The ideal candidate pairs a solid understanding of computer systems — host software, firmware, buses and the high-speed interfaces between them, and the board underneath all of it — with solid programming ability, hands-on hardware debug skill and a dedication to quality. You are comfortable driving a board or system under real workload rather than only measuring it, and you want to see your test catch a defect before a customer does.

Key job responsibilities

job.name: System Verification Engineering Intern
job.description:
Job Description

2027 Summer Internship

May 24, 2027 - August 13, 2027

Renesas Electronics’ Infrastructure Power team is looking for a talented Electrical or Computer Engineering

student to join our System Design team as a System Verification Engineering Intern in Austin, Texas.

Our team develops advanced digital power management controllers used in high-performance computing,

AI, and data center applications.

This internship provides hands-on experience with digital and system-level verification of complex power

management systems. The intern will work primarily with System Verilog-based verification

environments, simulation, test automation, regression testing, and waveform debugging, while

developing an understanding of digital control loops, power converters, and mixed-signal system behavior.

The selected candidate will work closely with digital design, verification, system, and analog engineers to

develop tests, debug issues, improve verification infrastructure, and characterize system behavior.

Job Responsibilities

  • Develop, maintain, and improve System Verilog-based testbenches for system-level verification of
  • digital power management controllers.
  • Develop automated tests to verify system functionality, including startup, configuration, controlloop operation, transient behavior, protection features, and fault recovery.
  • Develop checkers, assertions, monitors, and automated pass/fail mechanisms to improve
  • verification quality.
  • Run and analyze simulation regressions, identify failures, and support debugging of RTL and systemlevel issues.
  • Analyze simulation waveforms, logs, register activity, and internal signals to identify unexpected
  • behavior and isolate design or verification issues.
  • Use Python and scripting to automate simulation execution, result processing, data extraction,
  • reporting, and comparison.
  • Help improve verification coverage, regression efficiency, test reproducibility, and simulation
  • infrastructure.
  • Develop an understanding of digital feedback controllers, including reference and feedback
  • signals, error response, settling time, overshoot, and transient response.
  • Support characterization of digital control-loop behavior across different operating conditions and
  • configurations.
  • Assist with verification and modeling of interactions between digital logic and analog/mixed-signal
  • system components.
  • Document verification methodologies, test results, debug findings, and characterization results.

Qualifications

Turing supports customers in two ways: first, by accelerating frontier research with high-quality data, advanced training pipelines, plus top AI researchers who specialize in software engineering, logical reasoning, STEM, multilinguality, multimodality, and agents; and second, by applying that expertise to help enterprises transform AI from proof of concept into proprietary intelligence with systems that perform reliably, deliver measurable impact, and drive lasting results on the P&L.

Ideal Background:

This role is ideal for engineers who have built production systems at companies like Google, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Meta, or similar high-scale engineering organizations. We especially welcome graduates from top computer science programs such as Stanford, MIT, Carnegie Mellon, UC Berkeley, Georgia Tech, and comparable institutions — though exceptional experience and skill always take precedence over pedigree.

Project Overview:

As a Software Engineering evaluator, you will create cutting-edge datasets for training, benchmarking, and advancing large language models, collaborating closely with researchers. This includes curating code examples, providing precise solutions, and making corrections — with a primary focus on Python across backend services, data pipelines, and ML infrastructure, alongside JavaScript (including ReactJS), C/C++, Java, Rust, and Go. You will evaluate and refine AI-generated code for efficiency, scalability, and reliability, and work with cross-functional teams to enhance enterprise-level AI-driven coding solutions.

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?

  • Work on AI model training initiatives by curating code examples, building solutions, and correcting code — primarily in Python, with additional work in JavaScript (including ReactJS), C/C++, Java, Rust, and Go.
  • Evaluate and refine AI-generated code to ensure that it is efficient, scalable, and reliable.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to enhance AI-driven coding solutions against industry performance benchmarks.

  • Hypothesize on steps in the software engineering cycle (prototyping, architecture design, API design, production implementation, launch, experiments, monitoring, operational maintenance) and evaluate model capabilities on them.
  • Design verification mechanisms that can automatically verify a solution to a software engineering task.

job.name: Quality Assurance Engineer, Amazon Leo Console
job.description:
Description Do you want to shape the quality of a product that connects customers to the internet across the globe? Amazon's Leo Console team is looking for a Quality Assurance Engineer II to own the frontend quality of the Leo Console — the destination where customers discover, purchase, and manage their internet service. In this role, you will build test strategies and Playwright automation for a product that is actively expanding into new countries, giving you the chance to define scalable testing practices from the ground up. You will work closely with product managers, UX designers, and software developers to catch issues early, surface missed use cases during grooming, and raise the quality bar so that every feature meets customer expectations before it ever reaches production.

Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end testing of the Leo Console frontend experience, creating and executing test plans that cover functional, integration, and regression scenarios across multiple country launches.
  • Build and maintain automated test suites in Playwright, evaluate coverage ROI, and define strategies for when and what to automate — partnering with the development team to expand automation over time.
  • Participate in product grooming sessions alongside product managers and UX designers, providing the QA perspective to identify edge cases, clarify acceptance criteria, and flag risks before development begins.
  • Triage and prioritize bugs, perform root cause analysis, and drive defect resolution to reduce the number of issues that reach production.
  • Own testing runbooks and QA documentation for the team, ensuring processes are repeatable and scalable as the product grows into new markets.

A day in the life

You will start many mornings reviewing incoming bug tickets and prioritizing what needs attention, then shift into proactive work — writing test plans for upcoming features or extending Playwright automation. Expect to spend a good portion of your week in collaborative sessions with UX designers, developers, and product managers during grooming and sprint ceremonies, where your input directly shapes what gets built and how. Between those sessions, you will have heads-down time to execute tests, refine runbooks, and analyze quality metrics. This is an independent, self-directed role where you decide where your attention has the most impact.

Read the full description

As a Systems Development Engineer on EC2 Core Platforms Engineering, you'll lead the technical direction for how we launch new compute platforms, keep the core fleet healthy at massive scale, and automate the way we build, working at the seam between hardware and software.

You'll lead the bring-up and validation of new EC2 server platforms, driving the technical plan across Nitro firmware, operating systems, and provisioning. You'll also set the approach for diagnosing and reducing failures across the core fleet, working to eliminate whole classes of failure rather than individual instances. You'll partner with hardware engineering, Annapurna, and the Nitro component teams, working on some of the largest compute fleets in the world, where a single improvement in reliability or build automation compounds across millions of hosts.   • Lead the bring-up and validation of new server platforms that host cloud compute instances, owning the technical plan from early lab testing through production launch, and bringing in hardware, firmware, and Nitro experts where the work needs them.
  • Own the approach to reducing hardware and software failures across a large-scale server fleet. Use data to find root causes, and drive permanent fixes and mechanisms that eliminate entire classes of failure and improve reliability.
  • Design and lead the software and automation that streamline how new platforms are introduced, setting the standard for provisioning, deployment, and validation so platforms reach production faster and with a high quality bar.

job.name: Research Intern - AI Serving Systems and Hardware - Microsoft Research
job.description:
Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.

We are seeking Research Interns to work where AI serving workloads meet the systems and hardware that run them. Large-model inference is limited by that hardware and by how well the serving stack uses it. Our team works across this boundary, from serving software and graphics processing unit (GPU) communication, through GPU clusters and their interconnects, down to chip architecture, to make AI serving faster, more reliable, and cheaper to build and run. Open problems range from keeping a large serving system running at predictable performance when GPUs, links, or software components fail to designing chips that keep pace with rapidly evolving workloads.

Research Interns will take on a research project in this space, shaped around their background and interests. Expected deliverables include working prototypes or simulators validated on real hardware, measurement studies, and paper submissions to top-tier venues.

Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Measure and characterize large language model (LLM) inference workloads on state-of-the-art GPU hardware, including how they behave when parts of the system fail or degrade.
  • Build prototypes, simulators, or models that test new ideas in serving systems, fault tolerance, GPU communication, or AI hardware.
  • Compare new approaches against existing methods.
  • Document findings and prepare results for publication at top-tier venues.
  • Present the work to technical audiences, both internally and externally.

Qualifications Required Qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related STEM field.

Other Requirements

We are responsible for the Tax Engine platform, providing the core services that classifies and calculate taxes (sales tax and VAT) for all Amazon sales, physical and digital, globally. We seek to interpret legislative texts and reason with the vast catalogue of Amazon goods, to compute the correct tax amounts to customers when they place their Amazon order. You will guide other Applied Scientist , MLE and SDE in exploring solutions through the application of Scientific techniques. You will evaluate risk areas other undertake new PoC and collaborate with other Amazon organization to create best in class solutions.

You will help us innovate different ways to enhance tax experience for our global customers.

You will need to be entrepreneurial, work in a highly collaborative environment with SDEs, Product managers and businesses. We like to move fast, experiment, iterate and then scale quickly, thoughtfully balancing speed and quality.

job.description:
Description We are seeking a talented Data Engineer to join Amazon's Traffic Engineering organization in developing next-generation bot detection and mitigation capabilities. As a Data Engineer, you'll be at the forefront of revolutionizing how we understand and leverage Traffic data used in Bot detection and mitigation.

This is a critical challenge at the intersection of ML and cybersecurity. With GenAI/LLM-powered bots now capable of mimicking human behavior, evading traditional detections, and monetizing attacks, we must revolutionize our approach from reactive to real-time protection. Your expertise will solve crucial challenges in data processing and analytics. Imagine building the pipelines that transform raw traffic data into actionable insights. You'll tackle complex problems like real-time data processing, ensuring data accuracy across multiple platforms, and creating scalable solutions that can handle exponential growth in data volume.

As the bridge between raw data and meaningful insights, you'll work with a diverse array of technologies, including Python, EMR, Spark,and Airflow, along with AWS services like Glue, Athena, and Redshift. But what truly sets this role apart is the opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams – from Scientists to Software Engineers to Program/Product – ensuring that your technical solutions align perfectly with business needs.

Your contribution will extend beyond just building data pipelines. You'll be a key player in maintaining data governance and compliance, implementing sophisticated access controls, and ensuring data security through encryption and audit mechanisms. This role demands not just technical expertise, but also the ability to think strategically about data architecture and its impact on business outcomes.

This role offers the unique opportunity to implement first-of-its-kind real-time behavior-based ML models that will safeguard Amazon's global infrastructure. Your work will directly impact millions of customers by ensuring the integrity and availability of Amazon's digital presence while advancing the state-of-the-art in automated threat detection and response.

job.name: Applied Scientist, Selling Partner Support Engagement
job.description:
Description Amazon's Selling Partner Support handles tens of millions of contacts annually worldwide. Our science team is transforming this experience by building AI agents that autonomously resolve seller issues, learn from every interaction, and continuously improve with minimal human intervention. These agents reason and adapt — from understanding the seller's context and selecting the right solution, to routing contacts optimally and automating resolution end-to-end. We do this in deep partnership with multiple engineering and product teams.

We are looking for an Applied Scientist who is excited to work on reinforcement learning, agentic architectures, and large-scale production systems. You will be directly connected to the problems sellers face every day, translating real customer pain into science solutions that operate at massive scale. You will frame ambiguous business challenges as tractable machine learning problems and ship systems that measurably improve millions of seller interactions.

Key job responsibilities

  • Optimize cost of agents in runtime by exploring deployment and domain adaptation of System One models.
  • Own research and development of reinforcement-learning based agent improvement systems, from problem formulation through production deployment and impact measurement.
  • Design approaches to preference learning, reward modeling, and policy optimization for conversational agents operating over real-world tools and APIs.
  • Build evaluation frameworks that measure agent quality across dimensions such as helpfulness, correctness, and safety.
  • Collaborate with engineering and product teams to deploy models into production systems serving sellers worldwide.
  • Contribute to the team's scientific impact through peer review, mentorship, and publications at peer-reviewed venues.

A day in the life

You read the latest research papers and implement new techniques by building rapid prototypes using AI-assisted coding tools, then take what works from prototype to production. You collaborate closely with product managers and engineering teams to translate seller pain points into deployed science solutions. You work with senior scientists to propose experiments and make the case for what to build next. You also stay connected to the seller experience by understanding the real problems sellers face so your models solve what actually matters.

job.description:
Title: Program Manager, Pilot Strategy & Analytics

Location: Austin, TX (hybrid)

Duration: 12+ months

Compensation: $55-75/hr

Work Requirements: US Citizen, GC Holders or Authorized to Work in the U.S.

ABOUT THIS FEATURED OPPORTUNITY

This role is the analytical backbone of the RCC commercial pilot portfolio. Working with program managers and with partners in Commercial, Finance, Reporting, and site operations, the person in this role:

  • defines what success looks like before a pilot launches
  • builds the test design that will prove it
  • creates and analyzes the data each pilot needs
  • delivers findings that leaders can act on

The work directly informs which programs scale across RCC worldwide.

Responsibilities:

  • Stitch Pilot Support Cross-functionally: Lead weekly control tower aligning RCC strategy optimization, business operations, workforce management, training, and field teams on pilot operations
  • Sequencing: Build and maintain the pilot roadmap. Schedule four to eight pilots across geographies so they don't depend on or collide with each other, don't overlap test populations, and fit around staffing, product launches, and peak seasons.
  • Measurement: Before each pilot launches, define:
  • the hypothesis
  • the primary metrics and guardrail metrics (e.g., NPS, revenue, conversion, adoption of new purchase options, ecosystem adoption, handle time)
  • the baselines and the success thresholds
  • A/B testing: Design test and control setups that work in a people-powered operation, such as randomizing by contact, Specialist, team, site, or market, holdouts, and staggered rollouts. Use power analysis to set sample sizes and test lengths. When clean randomization isn't possible, use other methods (e.g., difference-in-differences, matched controls).
  • Data generation: Where data doesn't already exist, design and set up ways to capture it so every pilot produces data that can be measured. Examples include observation and tagging frameworks, Specialist and customer surveys, feedback loops, and pilot tracking logs.
  • Structured and unstructured analysis: Analyze two kinds of data together to explain both what happened and why:
  • structured data, like transactions, contacts, workforce data, and KPIs
  • unstructured data, like call and chat transcripts, survey verbatims, Specialist and customer feedback, and field observations
  • Refinement: Watch pilots while they run, flag issues early, and recommend changes along the way. Lead a readout at each stage gate that ends in a clear scale, refine, or stop recommendation.
  • Storytelling: Build executive-ready readouts that lead with the answer, quantify impact and how confident we are in it, and make tradeoffs explicit, including how results differ across geographies.
  • Repeatability: Build reusable dashboards, templates, and a measurement playbook so each pilot evaluation is faster and more consistent than the last.

job.name: Machine Learning Engineer
job.description:
Your Job The ML Engineer will build physics-informed surrogate models on Azure Machine Learning that predict engineering simulation outcomes directly from design parameters. They will be pre-screening candidate designs in milliseconds so only the most promising ones require full high-fidelity simulation, accelerating the design-optimization cycle.

Our Team Established in 1938, Molex delivers comprehensive electronic solutions for various markets, including data communications, telecommunications, consumer electronics, industrial, automotive, commercial vehicle, aerospace and defense, medical, and lighting. You'll join the platform team behind our Azure AI/ML engineering tools, partnering closely with data scientists, LLM engineers, and MLOps teams to keep GPU-heavy training and simulation workloads reliable and fast.

What You Will Do

  • Design and train surrogate models (neural networks, Gaussian processes, gradient-boosted trees, GNNs/PINNs) on Azure GPU compute (ND/NC series).
  • Incorporate physics-informed constraints so predictions stay physically valid, not just statistically fit.
  • Build model-uncertainty and confidence scoring to decide which designs need full simulation validation, then retrain as new results arrive.
  • Deploy and version models via Azure ML endpoints and model registry; monitor for drift on a rolling basis.
  • Benchmark surrogate vs. full-simulation speedup to guide platform-level performance tuning.

Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

  • Extensive hands-on experience building, training, and deploying ML models in production — not just using pretrained APIs.
  • 10+ years building ML for physical/engineering systems (surrogate modeling, physics-informed ML, or scientific ML).
  • Strong Python with PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Understanding of relevant engineering/physics fundamentals and simulation data formats for your domain.
  • Experience with Azure Machine Learning or a similar cloud ML platform.
  • Familiarity with uncertainty quantification (Bayesian approaches, ensembling).

What Will Put You Ahead

  • Direct experience with industry-standard EM or physics simulation tools.
  • Geometric deep learning (graph neural networks, mesh-based models) for CAD data.
  • Background in RF/high-speed electronics or interconnect design.

The Position Forward Deployed Engineers sit inside the client’s problem, not next to it. You embed with an enterprise team, help find the work that actually warrants AI, learn to architect the system, build it, and stay long enough to help make it survive contact with production.

This is a three-way role: consultant, operator, engineer. You will grow into pressure-testing a business case with a COO or VP of Engineering while learning to diagnose why retrieval quality collapsed after a data refresh. The people who succeed here are fast learners who join discovery conversations on Monday and help ship what was scoped on Thursday.

On this track, your focus is data, retrieval, and model behavior : you help make agents trustworthy by getting the data, context, and evaluation right.

We work with regulated industries and Fortune 500 clients who have AI mandates, real constraints, and low tolerance for demos that don’t hold up.

How We Approach The Work FDEs are trusted to help shape the solution, not only deliver it. Every engagement calls for sound judgment, which you will develop over time:

  • Reframes the request. Treats “we need an agent for X” as a hypothesis, not a spec.

job.name: Data Engineer, Amazon Traffic Engineering
job.description:
Description We are seeking an experienced Data Engineer to build and operate the Core Data Infrastructure that underpins our ML and Science initiatives for Bot Management. You will design and own production-grade data pipelines that ingest billions of events from diverse source systems and transform raw signals into ML-ready feature groups that Science and ML Platform teams depend on for training, evaluation, and inference.

This is a hands-on engineering role at the center of a fast-moving ML organization. Our Science teams build increasingly sophisticated models, each requiring different data formats, latencies, and serving patterns. You will build the pipelines and feature infrastructure that make this possible: ingesting from Trails and Non-Trails sources, transforming disparate datasets into versioned feature groups, and operating the Feature Store that serves features consistently across all model types. You will partner directly with Applied Scientists to translate model data requirements into reliable pipelines, and work across data engineering, software engineering, and science teams to deliver data that is accurate, timely, and well-governed.

Key job responsibilities

Data Pipelines & Ingestion — Build and own batch and near real-time pipelines spanning Trails (raw and aggregated) and Non-Trails sources (Clickstream, Customer Segmentations, OPS). Evolve pipelines from Cradle/POC to production-grade using AWS Glue. Implement data quality checks, drift detection, and governance frameworks.

Feature Engineering & Serving — Build versioned feature groups across multiple storage backends (S3 for tabular data, OpenSearch for embeddings). Develop production pipelines that transform raw signals into ML-ready features, and help operate the Feature Store that serves them consistently to Science teams.

Streaming & Real-Time Systems — Develop and operate Apache Flink applications and stream processing for near real-time feature computation. Build event-driven data flows leveraging Kinesis and Kafka to support low-latency bot detection signals.

Science Partnership — Partner with Applied Scientists and ML Platform engineers to define data contracts and SLAs, understand model data requirements, and ensure feature pipelines integrate cleanly with training and inference systems.

Operational Excellence — Own the reliability, monitoring, and cost efficiency of the pipelines you build. Participate in on-call, root-cause data issues, and drive improvements that reduce operational load.

Description Come change the way the world sees the Cloud!

The CloudWatch Logs team builds and manages some of the largest logging systems in the world. CloudWatch Logs allows AWS users to ingest their application and AWS logs in a highly scalable, durable, and reliable service for enterprise scale; find and analyze the right log data to solve operational problems; generate metrics and alarms from their log events; or send log data to other downstream systems.

On the Logs team you’ll get to build critical monitoring services that impact every single AWS customer, both internally and externally – there’s not many team’s that can say that!

This is a full-stack development position, leaning towards back-end work.

Key job responsibilities

  • Collaborate with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to conceive, design, and bring innovative products and services to market.
  • Design, build and lead innovative technologies in a large distributed computing environment
  • Create solutions to increase ingestion of telemetry data at scale and speed.
  • Build distributed ingestion, processing, storage, index, and query systems that are scalable, fault-tolerant, low cost, and easy to manage/use.
  • Design and code the right solutions starting with broadly defined problems.
  • Work in an agile environment to deliver high-quality software.

About The Team Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services is redefining how the world stores, serves, and reasons over data in the age of AI. Our vision is to make every byte of enterprise data instantly durable, infinitely scalable, and intelligent by default — so that organizations of any size can turn their data into insight and action. We pair decades of hard-won operational experience with relentless curiosity to build the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on: object storage (Amazon S3), block storage (Amazon EBS), archival storage (Amazon S3 Glacier), analytics and database engines (Amazon Redshift, EMR, SageMaker), and the ultra-high-performance caching layers that make generative AI and analytics fast and trustworthy at enterprise scale. We're hiring Principal and Senior Principal Engineers across the org to own technical direction for some of our hardest problems: building a new cache product purpose-built for GenAI and analytics — delivering ultra-low-latency, ultra-high-throughput access to S3 data at exponential scale; setting architecture for S3 storage at the exabyte tier; and driving the engineering direction of SageMaker, Redshift, EMR, and AWS Database Services. These are deep, high-ownership systems roles — some remote-eligible, others anchored to hubs like Seattle, Irvine, and Berlin — for engineers who have led org-wide technical strategy and want to see it run in production. If you want to build systems that operate at planet scale — where durability, availability, latency, and failure-mode ownership are first-class concerns measured in eleven nines — this is the team.

What You'll Do

This is a rare chance to own and ship the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on — not features on top of a platform, but the storage, data, and caching layers that everything else depends on, operating at a scale no one else in the industry touches. You'll architect systems that store and serve exabytes of the world's most critical data, where a single design decision ripples across hundreds of millions of customers and millions of applications.

The problems here are unlike anywhere else. How do you deliver eleven nines of durability while adding net-new capabilities to a service that already stores hundreds of trillions of objects? How do you build a new cache product that serves S3 data at ultra-low latency and ultra-high throughput for GenAI and analytics workloads growing exponentially? How do you evolve block, object, and archival storage — and the analytics and database engines on top of them — without ever compromising the durability, availability, and latency guarantees customers have bet their businesses on? These are deep systems challenges solved in production, at a scale where the usual playbooks break down. You help write the new ones.

job.name: Salesforce Developer
job.description:
Our Mission SPAN is enabling electrification for all ⚡ We are a mission-driven company designing, building, and deploying products that electrify the built environment, reduce carbon emissions, and slow the effects of climate change.

  • Decarbonization is the process to reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions, especially carbon dioxide, from entering our atmosphere.
  • Electrification is the process of replacing fossil fuel appliances that run on gas or oil with all-electric upgrades for a cleaner way to power our lives.

At SPAN, We Believe In

  • Enabling homes and vehicles powered by clean energy
  • Making electrification upgrades possible
  • Building more resilient homes with reliable backup
  • Designing a flexible and distributed electrical grid

The Role We are looking for a Salesforce Developer to build and own the automation, data model, and custom functionality behind SPAN's commercial operations. This is a hands-on build seat: you will design and ship record-triggered and screen Flows, model custom objects and relationships, write Apex and Lightning Web Components where a declarative approach won't scale, and deploy your work across sandboxes to production with change-management rigor. You will work directly with Sales, Operations, Finance, and Supply Chain stakeholders to turn business processes into scalable Salesforce solutions.

This role supports all channels of the SPAN commercial team, including our CPQ/quoting pipeline, Lead Pass routing, installer and builder portals, and the order-to-fulfillment integration.

Responsibilities

  • Design and build Salesforce automation end to end, primarily in Flow (record-triggered before/after-save, screen flows, subflows, invocable actions), with bulk-safe, recursion-aware design.
  • Model and maintain custom schema: custom objects, junction objects, master-detail and lookup relationships, record types, and validation rules.
  • Write Apex (triggers, controllers, test classes) and build Lightning Web Components when declarative tools can't meet the requirement, with proper test coverage.
  • Gather requirements from cross-functional stakeholders, author design specs and release documentation, and translate business process into documented, scalable solutions.
  • Own deployments across multiple sandboxes to production using Gearset, following SPAN's change-management and release-documentation conventions.
  • Maintain and extend the security model: permission sets, field-level security, profiles, and sharing.
  • Support and enhance the core commercial surfaces: CPQ/quoting, Lead Pass, installer/builder Experience Cloud portals, and the Salesforce side of the order/fulfillment integration.
  • Use AI to work with greater leverage, both to increase your own delivery velocity (e.g., AI coding assistants to ship Apex/LWC faster) and to build AI-enabled solutions (Agentforce, Einstein, prompt-driven automation) that streamline Sales and Sales Operations processes.

Preferred Skills And Experience

About Salesforce Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. Behind every Salesforce AI agent is a model, and behind every model is infrastructure that has to be fast, cheap, and secure. We’re building the Kubernetes-based platform that serves those models: a large and fast-growing fleet of custom models handling massive volumes of LLM traffic across multiple public clouds. You’ll join the Hyperforce Container Platform (HCP) team and build the layer beneath the models: GPU scheduling, distributed inference, and model serving.

  • Treat AI as a first-class workload. Secure and operate it on the same service mesh, workload identity, and caching layer as every other Salesforce service.
  • Build the agentic runtime layer. Work on multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), knowledge graphs, and evaluation for accuracy and safety.
  • Isolate untrusted workloads. Build sandboxing for AI agents and the code they generate, keeping production workloads separated from each other.
  • Own reliability end to end. Run services to a 99.99% availability SLA, and make the platform observable and self-healing at fleet scale.
  • Shape the open-source foundations. Contribute upstream to vLLM, llm-d, Ray, and Kueue, Agent Substrate, and influence their direction and roadmaps.

SentiLink helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role SentiLink's Information Security team protects our systems, data, and customers while enabling the business to move quickly and securely. We operate a modern, AWS-based environment and support security and compliance programs including FedRAMP, SOC 2, and PCI DSS.

We're looking for a Senior Cloud Security Engineer to own and improve the technical security implementation of SentiLink's AWS GovCloud environment. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on building, maintaining, and operating security controls—not a compliance or audit-management position.

You'll work across AWS infrastructure, Kubernetes, identity and access management, security tooling, vulnerability management, and monitoring. You will partner closely with Infrastructure, Security Engineering, IT, and our Security & Risk team to turn security and FedRAMP requirements into effective, maintainable implementations. job.name: Systems Engineer - Network Software Performance
job.description:
About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC, About The Team Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare's network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers' traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves.

Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum).

We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.

Hiring Department: Applied Research Laboratories

Position Open To: All Applicants

Weekly Scheduled Hours: 40

FLSA Status: Exempt from FLSA

Earliest Start Date: Immediately

Position Duration: Expected to Continue

Location: PICKLE RESEARCH CAMPUS

Design, develop, test, document and maintain Linux systems engineering with security controls for modern TCP/IP networked systems in the Advanced Technology Laboratory (ATL).

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Computing Technologies or other related discipline.

  • Demonstrated ability to follow coding standards and testing standards.
  • Experience with Linux and open source tools for creation, testing, version control and documenting Linux configuration and associated security controls.
  • Knowledge of networking and computer security concepts.

US Citizen. Selected applicant is subject to government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information at level appropriate to project requirements of the position.

job.name: Senior Cloud Security Engineer, FedRAMP
job.description:
SentiLink helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role SentiLink's Information Security team protects our systems, data, and customers while enabling the business to move quickly and securely. We operate a modern, AWS-based environment and support security and compliance programs including FedRAMP, SOC 2, and PCI DSS.

We're looking for a Senior Cloud Security Engineer to own and improve the technical security implementation of SentiLink's AWS GovCloud environment. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on building, maintaining, and operating security controls—not a compliance or audit-management position.

You'll work across AWS infrastructure, Kubernetes, identity and access management, security tooling, vulnerability management, and monitoring. You will partner closely with Infrastructure, Security Engineering, IT, and our Security & Risk team to turn security and FedRAMP requirements into effective, maintainable implementations. You should be comfortable independently identifying gaps, designing pragmatic solutions, and following through on implementation and ongoing operation.

This is an individual contributor role with meaningful technical ownership and no people-management responsibilities.

job.name: Principal DevOps Engineer
job.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the Role

SambaNova is hiring a DevOps Engineer for SambaNova’s SambaSuite platform.

We are helping enterprises and service providers build their AI inference platforms for end users, powered by our state-of-the-art RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) hardware architecture . Our cloud-agnostic, enterprise-grade MLOps platform abstracts infrastructure complexity and enables seamless deployment, management, and scaling of foundation model workloads at production scale.

As a DevOps Engineer, you will take ownership of our CICD pipelines and help build a robust and scalable release infrastructure across our components.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role working at the intersection of AI infrastructure, enterprise software, and developer experience.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable infrastructure and deployment pipelines for enterprise AI platforms
  • Architect and implement robust CI/CD pipelines using tools such as CircleCI , GitHubActions etc ensuring stability, scalability, and performance
  • Optimize CICD workflows, including configuration management and integration with build systems
  • Drive SRE practices including monitoring, observability, alerting, incident response , and post-mortems
  • Deploy and manage Kubernetes clusters and maintain Helm charts for application deployments
  • Design and implement infrastructure solutions using GCP services.
  • Establish and enforce infrastructure-as-code standards using tools like Terraform , etc.
  • Collaborate with development teams to optimize build, test, and deployment processes
  • Lead capacity planning, disaster recovery and SecOps workflows
  • Automate operational workflows and reduce toil through intelligent tooling and process improvements

Develop software and automation that make this data accessible and searchable. Own defined components

job.name: Software Development Engineer, Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management
job.description:
Description Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management (LIM) Operations Tooling team builds the products that run the Leo network day to day. Our tools are used by the Network Operations Center, Call Leaders, and service teams across Networking, Commerce, and Satellite Operations to see the health of the network, catch problems before customers do, coordinate fast when something goes wrong, and automate the work that slows operators down.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

job.name: Systems Engineer, AWS Incident Response
job.description:
Description As a Systems Engineer on AWS Incident Response, you will be on the front line of AWS incident response. You will lead high-severity calls, triage complex failures across distributed systems, coordinate resolver teams, and drive incidents to mitigation in real time while millions of customers depend on the outcome. Between incidents you will obsess over metrics and detection analysis, building dashboards and mechanisms that surface problems before customers notice, and you will drive operational improvements that make the incident management ecosystem faster and more accurate.

You will make real-time decisions under pressure, deep-diving the largest and most complex technical environment in the world. You will develop expertise across AWS services, networking, and infrastructure, building a breadth of knowledge that few roles offer. Your scope spans all of AWS rather than a single service. You will own operational processes end to end and use data to find the next improvement in how we detect and mitigate faster. You will also have the opportunity to grow your development skills by taking on coding projects that accelerate incident response and reduce toil.

This role includes participation in an on-call rotation covering weekdays, weekends, and holidays. On-call shifts fall within your local daytime hours.

Key job responsibilities

  • Lead high-severity incident response calls end to end: assess impact, coordinate resolvers across AWS service teams, communicate clearly under pressure, manage escalations, and drive the incident to mitigation with documentation throughout.
  • Own and run operational health reviews, and build and maintain the dashboards, metrics, and monitoring that surface trends before they become incidents.
  • Improve detection accuracy and speed. Identify patterns across events and build proactive mechanisms that prevent recurrence.
  • Deep-dive operational data to find systemic issues, measure response effectiveness, and prioritize improvements against what the data shows is degrading.
  • Identify gaps in operational processes, documentation, and tooling, and build or improve mechanisms that reduce time-to-detection and time-to-mitigation.
  • Apply scripting, automation, and generative AI to accelerate incident response and reduce toil, including where AI can augment human judgment during an incident or surface insight from operational data at scale.
  • Work with service teams so that learnings from each incident drive corrective actions to completion, closing the loop between what broke and what gets fixed.
  • Mentor peers in your areas of technical and operational strength.

A day in the life

job.name: Senior Software Engineer - HW/SW in Fleet Infrastructure
job.description:
Overview The Operating Systems and Server team within the Microsoft 365 Core Platform is responsible for improving the reliability, security, compliance, and operational health of the infrastructure that powers Microsoft 365 services worldwide.

Our team builds intelligent systems and automation that keep one of the world’s largest cloud fleets secure, current, and resilient. We focus on operating system lifecycle management, firmware health, security and patch freshness, vulnerability remediation, fleet compliance, and safe deployment of critical platform updates across hyperscale infrastructure.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will design, build, and operate large-scale distributed systems that analyze fleet telemetry, identify security and freshness risks, and drive automated remediation across Microsoft 365 infrastructure. You will work at the intersection of cloud engineering, operating systems, firmware, security, data platforms, and AI-assisted operations to improve the trustworthiness and reliability of the services millions of customers depend on every day.

You will partner closely with security teams, hardware and firmware engineering, Azure infrastructure and Fleet management teams, service owners, and site reliability engineers to deliver solutions that improve platform health, reduce operational risk, and ensure Microsoft 365 infrastructure remains secure, compliant, and up to date.

The team operates a dedicated lab environment used to The lab enables realistic testing of hardware and software configurations, rollout safety mechanisms, telemetry, failure scenarios, and remediation workflows.

Enabling our success in these objectives is our lab environments, where we validate new server platforms, deployment processes, operating system changes, and firmware updates before they are introduced into production.In this role, This role will encompass lab management, including server inventory, capacity planning, hardware installation and retirement, configuration consistency, test readiness, and documentation. You will partner with hardware, firmware, networking, security, and deployment teams to ensure the environment remains representative, reliable, secure, and available for engineering validation.

You will also apply practical networking knowledge to configure and troubleshoot lab infrastructure, including top-of-rack switches (ToRs), VLANs, load balancers, virtual IP addresses (VIPs), routing, addressing, connectivity, and related network dependencies. Success requires the ability to diagnose issues across server, firmware, operating system, deployment, and network layers and to drive problems through resolution.

job.name: Senior Site Reliability Engineer I
job.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact Every body camera upload. Every piece of digital evidence. Every chain of custody log that holds up in court. That's us. Axon's Platform team is the engine behind what hundreds of thousands of officers rely on every day. We're one of the world's largest blob storage customers, ingesting tens of petabytes of video and that number keeps climbing. Audio, photographs, sensor streams: if it's evidence, we move it, store it, and protect it. We're not in maintenance mode. We're in build mode. We're modernizing from the ground up with Kubernetes native lifecycle management, GitOps driven configuration, and infrastructure as code that actually reflects reality. We run a polyglot datastore environment: relational databases, wide column stores, document stores, caches, and queues and we're building the self service platform that helps every team at Axon pick the right tool and use it well. Kafka moves the data. Terraform provisions the world. Grafana tells us when something's wrong before our users do. You'll set technical direction across all of it. Not just implementing someone else's plan, but making the calls: which datastore patterns we standardize on, how we design for scale and failure, where we invest in automation versus buy versus borrow. You'll partner with teams across Axon who are building on top of our platform, and your architectural fingerprints will be on systems that process evidence for millions of people.

Location - This role is based out of our Atlanta, Seattle, or Boston office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.

What You'll Do

job.name: Lead Security SRE
job.description:
Company Overview Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM).

What you'll do

job.description:
Description Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

We are seeking an exceptional System Development Engineer for our Network Operations team within the Optical Inter-Satellite Link (OISL) organization. This is a high-impact role where you will be a key contributor to the Network Operations function of OISL — building and operating the tooling, automation, and monitoring systems that support a revolutionary laser communication network connecting thousands of satellites in space.

The Role

This is an individual contributor role. You will contribute to the end-to-end Network Operations capability for OISL, including building tools and services for monitoring and incident response, driving automation of operational workflows, and supporting operational readiness as the constellation scales. You will partner with engineers across the organization to develop solutions that improve laser link reliability and availability.

Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities

Network Operations Support & Execution

Support the OISL Network Operations strategy by contributing to tooling development, automation initiatives, and process improvements.

Participate in the NetOps on-call program: contribute to escalation workflows, automated ticketing, runbooks, and incident response.

Support operational cadence: assist with metrics reviews, readiness assessments, and capacity planning activities.

Automation & Tooling

Build scalable services that automate monitoring, fault detection, classification, and ticketing for the optical inter-satellite link network.

Develop data pipelines for KPI tracking, anomaly detection, and proactive issue identification.

Build observability platforms — dashboards, alerting, and real-time monitoring at scale.

Apply ML/AI for fault correlation, root cause analysis, and predictive failure detection.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with hardware, software, and ground network teams to support system reliability improvements.

Contribute to investigations into complex link failures and constellation-level fault patterns.

Participate in architecture reviews and program planning as a Network Operations representative

Individual Contribution.

Hands-on development of tools, services, and automation (Python, Spark SQL, cloud services).

job.name: Software Development Engineer, Agentic Workspaces
job.description:
Description AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Amazon WorkSpaces has protected and empowered enterprise work for over a decade and we are now reimagining what a workspace is. We are building Agentic WorkSpaces: a platform where the workspace itself is an active partner in how you work, not just infrastructure that delivers applications. Today more than a million users rely on WorkSpaces daily; tomorrow those workspaces will host AI agents alongside humans — agents that code, troubleshoot, analyze, and act on behalf of their users, governed by the same identity and security policies as the people they serve. We compete with Microsoft, Citrix, and Omnissa, and we intend to leapfrog them by building the workspace that was designed for the agentic era, not retrofitted for it.

Agentic Workspaces' On-Instance Software (OIS) is the layer that makes this possible from the inside of every WorkSpace: the operating-system provisioning logic, on-instance agents, telemetry, and update mechanisms across Windows and Linux. Our vision is for that software to be invisible — operating systems that launch within weeks of upstream general availability, agents that update themselves safely without disrupting access, provisioning that is self-diagnosable, and fleet management that works through the same AWS tools customers already use — delivered from commercial regions to classified partitions with automation as the default, so quality and breadth improve release over release.

Knowledge of Linux operating systems, Linux package management, and native Linux desktop application development is desired.

You want to solve challenging problems in operating systems, identity, AI, and desktop platform engineering at a scale that impacts more than a million users daily.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to design, build, and operate the services and agents that provision, secure, and maintain WorkSpaces for humans and increasingly for the AI agents that work beside them across every supported OS and identity provider. As a developer on our team, you'll own code end-to-end from design to development and work closely with senior technical leaders within the team and across AWS.

You will own end-to-end delivery of features and systems within OIS - from design through deployment and operations - holding a high bar for availability, latency, and security.

Read the full description

In this role, you will follow best practices of software development to ensure project schedules are met and software quality is high. You will create and review system designs and work with the team to build the service. You will actively participate in the team's planning and brainstorming to help us shape the future direction of our products. Our team is an AI first team and we leverage AI enabled tooling throughout the product lifecycle to enable us to deliver high quality product fast.
