AI Disclosure: As part of the application process, Artificial Intelligence will be used in the hiring process for this role Work Arrangement: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to the office three days per week, at minimum.

The Role The Data Engineering organization at General Motors is building a unified Vehicle Data Platform that moves data and configuration between vehicle ECUs and the cloud. Our team is the only team within General Motors that delivers software on every compute module the company has. Our software is delivered as libraries, apps, and services on Android, Linux, and QNX and covers four areas. The control plane retrieves configuration from the cloud and applies it across the vehicle's ECUs. The data plane collects, processes, and forwards data from vehicle systems to cloud storage. The SDK lets application teams use the platform. The unified logging infrastructure manages logs across the vehicle software stack.

We are looking for a Senior Software Developer to own features and components across these areas. You will take work from design through release and field support, write and review code, and mentor junior engineers. You will work with application, platform, cloud, cybersecurity, and privacy teams to deliver software on production ECUs with limited CPU, memory, storage, and bandwidth.

About Turing

Turing is one of the world’s leading AGI infrastructure companies, working with frontier AI labs to accelerate model development through high-quality training data, evaluations, and engineering talent.

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced, hands-on software engineers to help evaluate and improve AI coding models .

Rather than primarily building production applications, you’ll work with coding agents across real-world repositories and assess the quality of their work. You’ll review generated code and agent behavior, determine whether solutions are technically correct, identify failure modes, and create the evaluation signals and feedback used to improve model performance.

Think of the coding agent as another engineer whose work you’re reviewing: Can it understand the task? Did it choose the right approach? Is the resulting code correct, robust, and maintainable? Can you explain precisely where it succeeded or failed?

What You’ll Do:

  • Evaluate AI-generated code and solutions across real-world software repositories
  • Review agent behavior, tool usage, and code changes for correctness and quality
  • Identify technical errors, weak approaches, and recurring model failure modes
  • Compare model outputs and explain why one solution is better than another
  • Create and refine rubrics and evaluation criteria for coding tasks

  • Build and maintain pipelines and infrastructure supporting data generation, collection, and evaluation workflows
  • Synthesize findings from data work into clear write-ups, updates, and recommendations for the team
  • Collaborate closely with researchers and engineers to translate qualitative judgment into scalable processes

  • 5+ years of hands-on software engineering experience

job.description:
About Turing

Turing is one of the world’s leading AGI infrastructure companies, working with frontier AI labs to accelerate model development through high-quality training data, evaluations, and engineering talent.

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced, hands-on software engineers to help evaluate and improve AI coding models .

Rather than primarily building production applications, you’ll work with coding agents across real-world repositories and assess the quality of their work. You’ll review generated code and agent behavior, determine whether solutions are technically correct, identify failure modes, and create the evaluation signals and feedback used to improve model performance.

Think of the coding agent as another engineer whose work you’re reviewing: Can it understand the task? Did it choose the right approach? Is the resulting code correct, robust, and maintainable? Can you explain precisely where it succeeded or failed?

What You’ll Do:

  • Evaluate AI-generated code and solutions across real-world software repositories
  • Review agent behavior, tool usage, and code changes for correctness and quality
  • Identify technical errors, weak approaches, and recurring model failure modes
  • Compare model outputs and explain why one solution is better than another
  • Create and refine rubrics and evaluation criteria for coding tasks
  • Produce high-quality evaluation and preference data used to improve coding models
  • Build and maintain pipelines and infrastructure supporting data generation, collection, and evaluation workflows
  • Synthesize findings from data work into clear write-ups, updates, and recommendations for the team
  • Collaborate closely with researchers and engineers to translate qualitative judgment into scalable processes
  • Share clear, actionable findings with AI researchers and engineers

What We’re Looking For:

  • 5+ years of hands-on software engineering experience
  • Strong proficiency in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or another major production language
  • Experience working in substantial real-world codebases
  • Strong code-review skills and technical judgment
  • Ability to clearly explain why an implementation is correct, incorrect, or could be improved
  • Strong written communication
  • Experience using modern LLMs or AI coding tools

Experience with LLM evaluation, coding agents, RLHF, preference data, rubric design, or post-training is a plus, but not required.

Engagement Details:

  • Compensation: Market rate; please provide a specific hourly rate expectation
  • Availability: 40 hours/week preferred, with at least 6 hours of Pacific Time overlap
  • Type: Independent contractor
  • Duration: Approximately 3 months
  • Start: As soon as possible

Evaluation Process:

We tackle that challenge with Bazel, Buildkite, and infrastructure that keeps everyday development efficient. Our work gives teams a dependable path from a code change to a completed build, with fewer delays and less infrastructure troubleshooting.

About The Role As a Senior Software Engineer on Code Scalability, you will solve the engineering problems behind building software at DoorDash’s scale. A change deep in a monorepo can trigger work across many projects; your job is to make that work efficient, predictable, and easy to investigate when something goes wrong. Projects span Bazel configuration and tooling, Buildkite orchestration, build execution and caching, and the services that support them. You will identify where improvements matter most, make the technical decisions, and work with teams across DoorDash to put those changes into practice.

The impact of this role extends to every team that depends on our platform. Shorter queues give engineers more time to iterate, dependable pipelines prevent interruptions, and useful diagnostics help them get back to their work. You will measure progress through those outcomes, alongside the cost and maintainability of the infrastructure you own.

You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…

  • Evolve build and CI workflows for large monorepos, keeping feedback fast and changes manageable as dependencies, code volume, and the number of contributing teams grow.
  • Develop Bazel rules, toolchains, and integrations that keep builds reproducible and make shared build infrastructure easier for teams to adopt across large monorepos.
  • Improve Buildkite pipeline throughput and reliability by reducing queue times, addressing build bottlenecks, and making better use of CI compute capacity.
  • Reduce redundant build work through dependency analysis, incremental builds, caching, and parallel execution, balancing developer feedback speed with infrastructure cost.
  • Build developer tools that explain build failures and help engineers reproduce CI behavior locally, making troubleshooting faster and reducing support overhead.
  • Rethink what a build and CI platform can do with AI: move beyond reporting failures toward intelligent diagnosis, PR triage, automated recovery, and guidance that helps developers move forward.
  • Instrument and operate build and CI infrastructure. Use metrics and developer feedback to track latency, reliability, and resource usage, then address recurring infrastructure problems.
  • Lead platform improvements from design through rollout, partner with engineering teams on migrations, and mentor teammates through technical decisions and code reviews.

We’re Excited About You Because…

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Our team builds the Chromium-based browsing engine, remote rendering and streaming technology, and distributed services that manage browser sessions across Cloudflare’s global network.

You will work at the intersection of systems programming, distributed systems, and security. Engineers contribute across the product, collaborating on browser changes, service orchestration, observability, and build infrastructure.

Company Overview Docusign brings agreements to life. More than 1.8 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. As a Software Engineer Intern on the Signing Core Backend (SCORE) team, you will help re-architect Docusign's eSign branding capability into a centralized microservice that high-value customers rely on to deliver a consistent brand experience across the Docusign ecosystem. You will work with RESTful and gRPC interfaces so customers can define their brand identity once and reuse it across multiple Docusign products and features, including validating branding configurations before they are applied to accounts. You'll contribute to moving branding compute into a dedicated Azure-hosted service, improving reuse, iteration speed, and support for new enhancements in our Tier-0 branding platform.

This is an internship role for 12 weeks of duration. This position is an individual contributor role reporting to the Senior Manager, Software Engineering.

Responsibility

  • Collaborate with the SCORE team to design and implement a centralized branding microservice that powers cross-product brand consistency for eSign and related experiences
  • Build and evolve RESTful and gRPC APIs that allow customers and internal services to define, retrieve, validate, and apply branding configurations in a consistent way
  • Help migrate branding compute from legacy components into a dedicated Azure-based service, leveraging MSF patterns and standards for reliability and scalability
  • Work on features that improve branding validation, so customers can preview and verify their brand setup before it is applied to production accounts, reducing misconfiguration risk
  • Implement unit, integration, and end-to-end tests to ensure branding APIs and workflows are robust, observable, and safe for Tier-0 production use
  • Partner with adjacent product and engineering teams that consume branding data (e.g., other signing surfaces and services) to support reuse and consistent experiences across products
  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and sprint ceremonies; incorporate feedback from your mentor and teammates to grow your engineering skills

job.name: Associate - Asset Management Performance Attribution Reporting
job.description:
Job Title: Associate

Department : Asset Management – Investment Operations / Reporting

About Business line/Function: Asset Management Reporting is responsible for transforming validated investment, accounting, pricing, and reference data into accurate, timely, and compliant reports for clients, regulators, and internal stakeholders. The function supports multiple reporting types across asset classes, geographies, and regulatory regimes.

Position Purpose: The Validator role acts as the independent quality, control, and risk assurance layer within the Asset Management Reporting lifecycle. The role ensures that all reports produced are technically accurate, conceptually sound, methodologically consistent, and compliant with internal standards, client requirements, and regulatory expectations before final release.

The Validator is accountable for challenging outputs, validating assumptions, and preventing incorrect or misleading information from reaching clients or regulators.

Responsibilities Direct Responsibilities

  • Perform independent validation of reports produced by Processors, focusing on accuracy, completeness, consistency, and appropriateness.
  • Review calculations, methodologies, disclosures, narratives, and trends across reporting periods.
  • Execute second-level controls and formally evidence validation and sign-off.
  • Ensure outputs align with documented procedures, regulatory guidance, and client expectations.

Contributing Responsibilities

  • Challenge unusual movements, overrides, or explanations and ensure they are supported by facts and documentation.
  • Identify systemic issues, recurring errors, or control weaknesses and escalate with root-cause analysis.
  • Support internal audits, external audits, and regulatory reviews with clear explanations and evidence.
  • Provide feedback and guidance to Processors to improve overall quality maturity.
  • Contribute to strengthening control frameworks and standardization.

Technical & Behavioral Competencies Technical Competencies

  • Strong conceptual understanding of Asset Management Reporting, including performance, holdings, regulatory disclosures, and client reporting objectives.
  • Ability to interpret and validate complex data flows across investment, accounting, pricing, and reference data domains.
  • Solid knowledge of control frameworks, audit expectations, and risk management principles.
  • Capability to assess methodological appropriateness and not just numerical accuracy.

Behavioral Competencies

job.name: Software Engineer (Machine Control/OOD/OOP)
job.description:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.

Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Broadband Plasma (BBP) division is the market-leading optical inspection system used by logic, foundry, and memory customers to detect critical defects at advanced nodes. These tools combine broadband plasma technology with unmatched sensitivity and speed to support high-volume manufacturing.

What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.

  • Doctorate (Academic) with at least 2 years of experience OR Master's Degree with at least 2 years of experience OR Bachelor's Degree with at least 3 years of experience. Degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer engineering/computer science.
  • Expertise in object-oriented software design principles and skilled in Object Oriented languages including Java or C++ or Python.
  • Experience in designing, developing and debugging multi-threaded, parallel and distributed high-performance computing software applications.
  • Ability to design, develop and debug software to control hardware including any of the following: electro-mechanical systems, opto-mechanical systems, data acquisition hardware, servo control systems, or robotics.
  • Good communication and leadership skills.

Minimum Qualifications Doctorate (Academic) or work experience of 0 years , Master's Level Degree or work experience of 2 years , Bachelor's Level Degree or work experience of 3 years

About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

Total Rewards Base Pay Range: $136,300.00 - $199,900.00 Annually Primary Location: USA-CA-Milpitas-KLA

job.name: Staff Software Development Engineer – Wallet - Authentication
job.description:
Company Overview IDMe is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with IDMe once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with IDMe at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use IDMe to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. IDMe’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. IDMe is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

IDMe is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At IDMe, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

Role Overview IDMe is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to join the Wallet - Authentication team, which builds the core sign-in, registration, and account management experiences that over 170 million members rely on to access the IDMe identity wallet. Authentication is the front door to IDMe: every member journey begins with creating, signing into, or managing their Wallet. The team owns sign-in, registration, MFA, account recovery, password reset, and MyWallet, along with the real-time risk engine that keeps those flows secure, ensuring members can access their verified identity across numerous federal agencies, state governments, healthcare organizations, and consumer brands.

job.name: Staff Software Engineer
job.description:
The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

job.name: Senior Software Engineer, Identity & Access Management (FedRamp)
job.description:
The MongoDB Atlas team is a diverse group of contributors working together to help our users manage MongoDB at global scale. We are responsible for MongoDB Atlas: our database as a service offering and fastest growing product which allows users to deploy fault-tolerant, globally distributed MongoDB clusters in just minutes.

We're seeking a Senior Engineer to join the Atlas Identity and Access Management (IAM) team. IAM is a platform and a product team. We serve internal engineers by providing them a secure and durable suite of services, and we serve external customers by providing them user facing features and products. We are the owners of Atlas’ authentication (OAuth, SSO, Federated Identity) and authorization (RBAC, ABAC) systems, along with many others. The IAM team’s mission is to enable customers to securely build their applications with Atlas through our best in class user experience.

The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) is a US government-wide program that provides a standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud products and services. Our FedRAMP program requires that anyone who is accessing customer data or metadata inside the Authorization Boundary be a US Citizen on US Soil.

This role will be based remotely in the United States.

Role Responsibilities

  • Design, architect, build, and deliver core pieces of IAM
  • Lead projects from specification to delivery
  • Mentor and grow other team members
  • Improve our codebase, best practices, and design principles
  • Define your top priorities and focuses, communicate them, and execute against them
  • Lead and contribute to complex technical projects and initiatives

Candidate Profile

  • 5+ years experience of software engineering, primarily focused on backend systems
  • Proficient in a modern compiled programming language (Java, Go, C#, C++, etc.)
  • Willingness to learn JavaScript and/or TypeScript along with modern frontend technologies (React, Redux, etc.); prior experience a plus
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Desire to collaborate with colleagues and mentor fellow engineers
  • Is curious, collaborative, empathetic, and intellectually honest
  • Has a passion for problem solving and learning new things in the domains of computer science and software engineering
  • Experience building identity and access management systems such as authentication (OAuth, SSO), authorization (RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC), and login and registration systems a plus

Success Measures

  • In 1 week you'll have completed your first pull request
  • In 3 months, you'll have contributed to a large project
  • In 6 months, you’ll be leading the design and execution of your own project

Read the full description

job.name: Senior Fullstack Engineer, Finance Technology
job.description:
The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Who We Are At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me , Do the Right Thing , and Get Things Done . These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About The Opportunity We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Payments Team, based in the US. Payments is where OKX meets the real financial world. Our team has built and operates the infrastructure connecting OKX to dozens of payment channels across global markets, giving users deposit and withdrawal options that are fast, convenient, and — most importantly — trustworthy. That platform moves and safeguards user assets at institutional scale, continuously, across time zones and regulatory environments.

This is not a greenfield team looking for its footing. The team is established, the platform is in production at scale, and we are actively expanding — both in scope and in headcount. That combination is rare: you get the leverage of joining a growing team where your work visibly shifts the roadmap, along with the discipline that comes from a system already trusted with real money.

It's also an unusually good place to learn. Payments is a domain that's hard to pick up from the outside — every market has its own rails, its own settlement behavior, its own failure modes, its own compliance expectations. Here you'll work across a wide range of payment methods and channels, and you'll build the judgment that comes from operating financial systems where the stakes are real: how to design for correctness when money is on the line, how to reconcile, how to recover, how to keep a platform observable enough that you find problems before your users do.

You'll work closely with product managers, designers, and partner-facing teams, and you'll set the technical bar for the engineers around you — through design docs, code reviews, and the everyday habit of doing things properly when nobody's watching.

If you like the sound of a team where the problems are genuinely hard, the standard is high, and your opinion changes the outcome, we'd like to talk.

job.name: Staff Software Engineer, Backend (Observability)
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

The Observability team builds the platform every Affirm engineer relies on to understand the behavior and performance of our systems. Our platform ingests 200+ TB/day of metrics, logs, and traces from hundreds of services across 80+ Kubernetes clusters, and when a user's checkout fails, our data is how engineers find out why. Over the next year, we’re moving to wide events, with one context-rich event per request, improving the signal-to-noise ratio to make debugging faster. We’re also introducing log sampling and building observability best practices into agentic development and code review, so that AI-assisted code is well instrumented by default.

We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to be the technical lead for Observability. You’ll spend most of your time hands-on while defining the roadmap, driving cross-functional projects, mentoring a team of six engineers, and partnering closely with infrastructure and product teams.

What You'll Do

  • You will own the architecture of Affirm’s telemetry pipeline, balancing reliability, query performance, and cost at 200+ TB/day.
  • You will design log sampling strategies that significantly reduce volume and cost without losing the signal engineers need during incidents.
  • You will shape how observability fits into agentic development, so that AI coding agents and code review catch instrumentation gaps before code ships.
  • You will be responsible for setting technical strategy for your team on a year-long time scale, and help your team tie it together with critical, business-impacting projects.
  • You will collaborate across teams in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design & analytics to ensure technical sustainability, risks and trade-offs are well understood and managed.
  • You will act as a force-multiplier for your team through your definition and advocacy of technical solutions and operational processes.
  • You take ownership of your team’s operations and availability by ensuring you have the right monitoring, triage rotations, playbooks, polcities, testing and alerting in place to support “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
  • You will foster a culture of quality and ownership on your team by setting code review and design standards for your team, and advocating for them beyond your team through your writing and tech talks.
  • You will help develop talent on your team by providing feedback and guidance, and leading by example.

What We Look For

job.name: Marketplace Operations Engineer (Boca Raton / Toronto)
job.description:
About the role

We run a lead distribution business: traffic partners send us consumer leads, we enrich and validate them in real time, and route them to the buyer who wants them most. Every request is money moving, and the systems that move it are small, fast services that have to be right the first time.

This role owns those services end to end — the code, the integrations, and the partner relationships that depend on them. It is deliberately half engineering, half account management. Most of what looks like a configuration change is a commercial decision: which buyer gets a lead, what we’ll spend to enrich it, whose traffic runs which flow. You’ll be trusted to make those calls and to ship them the same day.

How you’ll work with the performance manager

A performance manager owns day-to-day performance: pacing, buyer health, source economics and media spend. You are their hands in the platform. They decide; you change the cap, budget, bid or filter the same day, correctly, without breaking anyone else’s flow.

You own the routing rules, the integrations, the code, and the technical side of every partner relationship. Enrichment and lookup spend is yours to decide. Media budgets are theirs.

What you’ll do

  • Build and maintain the real-time services that receive, score, enrich and distribute leads.
  • Own every third-party integration — lead platforms, consent and compliance providers, credit and data enrichment, communications — including the unglamorous parts: timeouts, retries, partner outages and bad payloads.
  • Update caps, budgets, bids and buyer filters (state, debt amount, accident recency and the like) on the performance manager’s request, same day. Keep the buyer/source matrix — states, prices, caps, windows, allowed sources, filters — current, so every change is made against the truth.
  • Own the technical leg of onboarding new traffic sources and buyers: write the posting spec, set up the org and campaign, send and verify test leads, and enable the integrations the deal needs (credit pull, phone validation, litigator/DNC scrub). Sales own paperwork and pricing until the test lead is verified; account management co-owns communication after go-live. You stay the partner’s technical point of contact.
  • Translate commercial requests into working configuration quickly, without breaking anyone else’s flow.
  • Decide what we spend to enrich a lead: when a lookup is worth paying for, which scores justify one, and the daily ceilings on enrichment spend.
  • Build and maintain lead-capture forms and landing pages, and keep every form field mapped to the buyer payloads it feeds.
  • Monitor production, respond to incidents, and know within minutes whether a drop in volume is us, the source, the buyer, or a cap or filter.
  • Pull the data behind billing disputes and buyer reconciliation: our records versus the buyer’s report versus what we invoiced, with internal margin and revenue stripped from anything that goes to a buyer.

Read the full description

job.name: Staff Full Stack Engineer - Lead
job.description:
We're partnering with a well established asset management firm, headquartered in Toronto. They operate across private equity, venture capital, real estate and private credit. With $45b in AUM and growing, they're expanding their team.

We're looking for a Staff Full Stack Engineer to join them on a permanent basis.

Our client is building its own portfolio management system for private equity teams, replacing a third-party PMS and supporting new funds from day one.

You will be the technical lead on the build: the most senior engineer on the team, setting the architecture and writing code yourself. You will lead a small engineering team, partner day to day with a product manager, and work with fund controllers, data operations and compliance.

Fund administrators remain the book of record, but this system drives cashflows, reconciliations, LP economics, performance and regulatory reporting. Correctness and auditability matter as much as speed.

What You Will Do

● Own the PMS architecture across data, workflow and controls, and reporting.

● Build the core workflows end to end: cashflow import, validation and four-eyes approval; NAV reconciliation against GP statements and administrator records; fee, carry and performance calculations; compliance rules; LP and regulatory reporting.

● Build platform controls as first-class features: maker-checker, period locking, version history, audit trails and entity-level access.

● Partner with the product manager, who owns the spec. Make sure it is complete, write the technical design, then build with AI coding tools.

● Make every build auditable: versioned calculations, lineage to source, and logged approvals and overrides.

● Lead the parallel run against the legacy system, resolve breaks, and gate each new fund's onboarding.

● Integrate with fund administrators, data extraction tools, the LP portal and downstream systems.

What You Will Bring

● 10+ years building production software, including 3+ years at staff or tech-lead level on systems where correctness is non-negotiable.

● Full-stack depth: backend services, data modelling and SQL, APIs and workflow design, and a modern web front end.

● Experience with financial or accounting-adjacent systems: ledgers, reconciliations, calculations that must tie out, and approval workflows.

● Cloud and data platform experience, ideally GCP.

● Daily use of AI coding tools, and a clear view on how to specify, review and test AI-generated code at team scale.

● Clear communication with non-engineers, especially product and finance teams.

Strong Plus

● Prior experience building or working on a PMS, investment accounting or fund administration platform, as a vendor or in-house. This is the most valuable background for the role.

● Private markets knowledge: capital calls and distributions, NAV, IRR, TVPI and DPI, fees and carry, side letters and LP restrictions.

job.name: Staff Platform Engineer
job.description:
We're partnering with a well established asset management firm, headquartered in Toronto.

They operate across private equity, real estate, private credit and venture capital.

They're looking for a Staff Platform Engineer to join them on a permanent basis.

With $45b in AUM and growing, this is an exciting time to join a progressive forward looking organisation.

You will own the shared platform that every AI product and agent runs on. The AI & Data team builds AI products for teams across the firm, from fundraising and finance to investing. Your job is to build the platform those products run on. You report to the Director of Engineering and are based in Toronto.

What You'll Own

● Data access and controls. Identity, authorization and audit for every app, MCP server and agent, so people and agents reach only the data they are entitled to.

● Context layer. A governed layer that turns the firm's knowledge, from relationship data to investment memos, data rooms and past deals, into context and memory that products and agents can use, within our retention obligations.

● Agent runtime. The shared foundation for agents: a shared registry of tools and skills, human approval for consequential actions, and the patterns teams use to ship agents.

● Evals and observability. How we measure quality, trace behaviour and gate releases across AI products.

● Shared services. Capabilities every product needs, such as notifications, shared UI components, and cost and model efficiency.

● Developer experience. Paved paths so every new product starts on the platform by default and developer token efficiency.

How They Build

● Decisions that are hard to reverse go through a written RFC and design review.

● They buy or adopt open source where the problem is a commodity, and build only what is specific to the firm.

● Agentic SDLC is the default. You use coding agents every day and raise the bar for how the team builds with them.

● You work with the security team from the start of every project.

● They move fast and focus on what delivers value, with a high bar on quality and no overengineering.

What You Bring

● 7+ years building production backend or platform systems including shared infrastructure other teams depend on and that you have kept reliable at scale.

● Production experience on GCP or another major cloud: serverless compute, managed data warehouses, IAM, encryption key management.

● Design experience in identity and authorization: OAuth and OIDC, service identity, delegated access, and policy engines such as Cerbos, OpenFGA, OPA or Cedar.

● LLM or agent systems shipped to production, including retrieval and knowledge systems, tool use and evals.

● Sound build-vs-buy judgment and clear technical writing, with RFCs that others can make decisions from.

● You act like an owner and stay pragmatic when things are uncertain.

What You'll Do

  • Design Kong Identity's plugin architecture enables custom grant flows, protocol extensions, and third-party integrations while maintaining security boundaries.
  • Drive implementation of compliance frameworks (SOC 2, FedRAMP, GDPR), including comprehensive audit trails, data residency controls, and privacy-preserving token designs.
  • Lead technical initiatives for Kong Identity's integration with observability platforms, supporting distributed tracing, metrics collection, and security event correlation.
  • Mentor engineering teams on advanced identity concepts including zero-trust architectures, workload identity, and service mesh integration patterns.

job.name: Software Development Engineer, Alexa Connections
job.description:
Description Do you want to shape how people stay connected across calls, text, and email? Alexa Connections is building a trusted communication agent that understands intent, context, and relationships, then acts on a customer's behalf to make every interaction feel natural. As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you'll design and deliver the software systems behind a context-aware assistant that grows more helpful over time. You'll work across the full software development lifecycle — from understanding customer problems, through system design and implementation, to deployment and operations — building privacy-first solutions that serve tens of millions of daily communication events.

Key job responsibilities

  • Design and implement software services that model each customer's personal connections graph, a privacy-first representation of relationships and communication patterns used to power context-aware assistance.
  • Build and operate scalable backend systems that integrate large language models and agentic reasoning to anticipate who, when, and how a customer wants to connect across calls, text, and email.
  • Collaborate with scientists, product managers, and peer engineering teams to translate research advances in personalization and memory into reliable, production-grade features.
  • Contribute to the full software development lifecycle — scoping, design, code review, testing, deployment, and operational support — while coaching teammates through constructive code reviews and documentation.
  • Identify and resolve root causes of operational issues, and continuously improve system reliability, maintainability, and performance.

A day in the life

Your morning might start with a design review for a new personalization feature, working through tradeoffs in scalability and data privacy with senior engineers and applied scientists. After lunch you could be writing and testing code for a service that ranks a customer's most relevant contacts, then pairing with a teammate on a code review. You'll regularly join standups with product managers and scientists to align on priorities, and you'll rotate through on-call responsibilities to keep the systems you build running smoothly.

About The Team The Alexa Connections team is growing, so you'll join early and help shape its engineering culture from the ground up. You'll work alongside experienced engineers and scientists who are invested in your growth, with mentorship and the chance to own meaningful problems. Our mission is to make communication effortless and trustworthy for customers worldwide, and we're focused on building intelligent, privacy-first systems that redefine how people stay in touch.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About The Role As Bedrock scales deployments nationwide, every machine we bring autonomy to has to be vetted, provisioned, calibrated, deployed, monitored, updated and serviced. Fleet Engineering builds the platform behind that lifecycle: the system of record, services and applications that teams across Bedrock use to run a fleet growing to thousands of machines. Many of these systems will be used by external partners as well.

The work crosses disciplines. One week you're architecting how we track sensor calibrations across every machine. The next, you're making a fault on an operator's tablet readable at a glance. You'll own problems end to end, working closely with technicians and operators in the field as well as multidisciplinary engineers across hardware, ML and robotics.

Also, you get to drive 100,000 lb excavators.

What You'll Do

job.name: Staff Software Engineer - Core Platform - Streaming & Storage
job.description:
StubHub is on a mission to redefine the live event experience on a global scale. Whether someone is looking to attend their first event or their hundredth, we’re here to delight them all the way from the moment they start looking for a ticket until they step through the gate. The same goes for our sellers. From fans selling a single ticket to the promoters of a worldwide stadium tour, we want StubHub to be the safest, most convenient way to offer a ticket to the millions of fans who browse our platform around the world.

We are seeking a Staff Software Engineer to join our Core Platform - Streaming & Storage team. In this role, you will lead the architecture and delivery of foundational streaming, messaging, and storage platforms that power P0 workflows across StubHub.

The team provides core engineering products used broadly across the company, including message queues, DLQ and retry infrastructure, messaging control planes, and storage platforms such as key-value databases, distributed caches, blob storage, and search/indexing systems. These platforms enable teams to build reliable, scalable, and event-driven services.

Today these platforms process 10–30 billion events per day for roughly 100 service teams. The team is at the beginning of a major program to bring StubHub's streaming home to AWS — consolidating from Azure services (EventHub, ServiceBus) onto a modern, Kafka-compatible platform with schema enforcement, self-service SDKs, and direct streaming and querying of event data from S3.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you will be the technical owner across our Streaming and Nonrelational Storage domains: setting technical direction, driving the key architecture and vendor decisions, ensuring operational excellence for P0 infrastructure, and mentoring the engineers who build and run it.

Location: Onsite (3 days in office/2 days remote) – New York, NY, or Aliso Viejo, CA What You'll Do

  • Own the technical strategy and architecture for StubHub's streaming platform and NoSQL/storage offerings
  • Lead the migration of streaming from Azure to an AWS-native, Kafka-compatible platform — vendor selection and benchmarking, broker deployment, schema registry, and producer/consumer SDKs
  • Design and operate high-throughput infrastructure processing billions of events per day, with reliability and performance appropriate to its company-wide blast radius
  • Drive engineering excellence: architecture and design reviews, observability, operational readiness, and incident response for P0 systems
  • Partner with ~100 service teams on adoption — migration guides, tooling, sign-off processes, and developer experience
  • Ensure compliance and governance (SOX, GDPR/CCPA) are designed into the platform, including PII handling, retention, and data access controls
  • Mentor and grow a team of 3–5 engineers, raising the technical bar through design review and coaching
  • Shape the team's multi-year roadmap in partnership with engineering

job.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

The CrowdStrike Cloud Detection Engine (CDE) team is building a powerful, next-generation platform designed to be a force multiplier for security teams. Our platform empowers customers who leverage multiple Falcon products to create and manage advanced, unified detections and content. This core platform capability is a strategic imperative for CrowdStrike, aiming to provide a competitive advantage that is difficult to replicate, ensuring our customers have unparalleled detection and response capabilities across the entire Falcon ecosystem.

We build the real-time data systems behind CrowdStrike's detection pipeline. Our team owns the streaming engine that processes all first-party sensor telemetry and maintains a petabyte-scale graph of real-time system activity, and the distributed correlation engine that evaluates trillions of events a day to catch multi-stage attacks that no single event can surface. Both systems are at the core of how CrowdStrike finds adversaries.

We're looking for someone who is excited about working in systems programming: custom query languages, graph databases, state machines, performance work where microseconds matter. Description & Requirements Our group

The BQL and Semantic Platform group builds the core query and semantic infrastructure used to access, analyze, model, and organize Bloomberg data.

The group develops the BQL engine, which powers Bloomberg Query Language and provides a common way to query and analyze data across Bloomberg. We also build the semantic platform used to define, manage, and materialize the semantic artifacts that describe Bloomberg data and the relationships between it.

Together, these capabilities provide the foundation for making Bloomberg data consistently queryable and semantically connected across products, applications, and emerging AI-driven use cases.

Our team

As part of Bloomberg’s investment in Semantic Technologies, we are building and operating Bloomberg’s RDF triplestore infrastructure.

Our team develops the database itself, working across the internals of graph storage and query processing rather than simply deploying or operating an existing database product.

Our work spans physical storage and indexing, SPARQL query planning and execution, transaction and isolation semantics, statistics and cardinality estimation, inference, replication, scalability, and operational reliability.

The platform stores semantic models and large RDF datasets used by engineering teams across Bloomberg. We are responsible for making billions of RDF statements efficiently queryable while providing the performance, correctness, availability, and reliability expected of enterprise-grade database infrastructure.

Our tech stack

RDF4J, LMDB, RocksDB, PostgreSQL, Java, Python, SPARQL, SHACL, RDF, Inferencing

You’ll need to have

  • 4+ years of professional software development experience
  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Hands-on experience developing database or graph database internals, rather than solely building applications on top of databases
  • Experience developing RDF triplestore, labeled property graph, or closely related graph database infrastructure
  • Strong understanding of several areas of database implementation, such as:

+ Storage engines, indexing, and physical data representation
+ Query planning, optimization, and execution
+ Transactions, concurrency, and isolation
+ Cardinality estimation and database statistics
+ Caching, memory management, and disk I/O
+ Replication, recovery, or high-availability architecture

  • Strong software engineering skills in Java or another systems-oriented programming language

job.description:
This is Adyen Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.

For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.

Senior Software Engineer, Issuing Team The Adyen Issuing product is an API-driven product for generating physical and virtual payment cards for business use cases. This enables our customers to benefit from the features of Mastercard and Visa cards such as interchange kickbacks, chargebacks, intelligent transaction declines, etc. B2B card transactions can be a safer and much cheaper alternative to bank or wire transfers.

The Chicago Issuing team is currently building a best-in-class dispute case management api. This is particularly interesting to our online travel agency customers who are exposed to risks of airlines and hotels going bankrupt between booking time and services rendered. By using Adyen issued cards, the travel agency can reverse a transaction by raising a dispute via the API. Additionally, as Adyen explores more credit-driven products, the case management API will serve as the main gateway for initiating automated fraud procedures related to charge cards and other financial products.

We are building a deceptively simple api that is scheme agnostic, and that hides the huge complexity of getting money back into our customers account. The issuing product has entered a phase of hyper-growth, and many new backend systems are currently being built to accommodate the 100x growth expected over the near term.

What You’ll Do

  • Work on complex technical projects from requirements analysis through design, implementation, testing and launch into production.
  • Bring your own point of view on best engineering practices.
  • Be hands-on and contribute to the implementation. Identify and improve parts of the platform to make it more robust and scalable.
  • Your code will be used at scale and you are expected to think in that mindset when building features.
  • We launch fast and iterate often. Concretely, this means that within your first few weeks, you will bring live functionalities that impact many merchants and shoppers.
  • Build APIs and tooling according to quality principles such as performance and code quality.
  • Collaborate across teams and time zones to get projects over the finish line.

Who You Are

What You'll Do

This role requires

  • 2+ years of professional experience in distributed SaaS software development.

About Swoop:

Swoop Technologies has a mission to organize and make accessible the world’s military and critical infrastructure. We are building a distributed operating system, SwoopOS, that decomposes the world’s equipment into a distributed robotic embodiment upon which a new generation of distributed systems, autonomous systems, and agentic AI can be built and deployed using our SDK, Valhalla, and operated via our browser, Surf. Imagine the world’s equipment - consisting of the electrical grid, communications architectures, manufacturing facilities, and militaries as a trapped supply of inputs possessing the potential to ensure Western military advantage, sovereign control of economically competitive manufacturing capacity, or the creation of a grid that fosters energy dominance. Swoop is liberating these trapped assets, allowing them to contribute to the world’s future as a series of building blocks to be combined at the speed of software, limited by only the hard constraints of physics and the soft constraints of safety. That is what Swoop is building. Not in the data center or cloud or edge on-premise computing node. In the physical world. This is a hybrid position that requires someone based in Minneapolis/St. Paul OR Washington, DC who can work in-office 3+ days per week

Impact:

Swoop’s operating system challenges many paradigms defining a scalable API. Management, security, and interoperability each will be re-imagined in how Swoop’s OS exposes interfaces to inputs and outputs within the stack. You will have a role developing APIs that Swoop developers leverage to build user-facing applications running on the Swoop platform. These APIs will be further leveraged and exposed to 3rd parties to develop an ecosystem of novel applications running on the Swoop OS.

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop and build new services and features, working closely internally with our firmware team to interface with the SwoopOS, our frontend team to support our web application, and our infrastructure team to deliver a stable product to market.
  • Design and build SDK’s for internal and external use, working with 3rd parties as they develop applications to run on our OS.
  • Author new Python packages for common functionality used across multiple services.
  • Ensure our services have strong availability and service level agreements across our code base, especially as it pertains to the runtime of our Kubernetes cluster in production.
  • Tune data storage configurations to optimize for scale and near real-time availability in a streaming architecture.

job.name: Business Analyst I, CMT
job.description:
Description Amazon.com operates in a virtual, global e-commerce environment without boundaries, and operates a diverse set of businesses worldwide, including Retail, third party marketplaces, e-commerce platforms, web services for developers. Amazon’s global price perception is how the population perceives Amazon’s pricing compared to other retailers. Elements that make up customer price perception include the perceived; (1) competitiveness of the retailers pricing (i.e. who has the perceived lowest prices), (2) clarity of price information on the site, (3) the price vs quality of the products offered (i.e. the value), (4) the price the customer expects to pay for the product at a given retailer, and (5) how Amazon messages pricing in press and advertising.

CMT Central Analytics team is responsible for the metrics and programs that define customer price perception today. The team is responsible for driving new initiatives to deepen our understanding and measurement of price perception, as well as delivering projects that will improve Amazon’s price perception overtime. We protect Amazon Customers and influence projects to improve price perception and price satisfaction.

Opportunity Do you want to be part of the team that ensures Amazon keeps its “best price” promise across millions of products worldwide? Does the challenge of driving decisions in a dynamic environment excite you? Do you love solving complex business problems using technology? Are you seeking an environment where you can drive innovation? Are you a passionate self-starter? If the answer to the above questions is a resounding “YES”, read on!

The ideal candidate is a motivated self-starter that can work in a fast paced, ambiguous environment with limited supervision. You must be a fast learner who can quickly absorb the nuances of Amazon's varied pricing programs and processes.

Amazon is one of the world’s most trusted companies. Help us keep it that way.

MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform for industrial and frontline teams. More than 15,000 customers , including McDonalds, Michaels, Cintas, Redimix, and U.S. LBM, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 16 million managed assets and 92 million completed work orders. In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining Autodesk Operations Solutions , the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations. Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours. About The Team Platform & Infrastructure keeps everything else fast, reliable and easy to build on. We own the shared services every product team builds on top of (identity, search, communication and our Pantry design system), the tooling that makes our engineers productive, and the release and runtime foundations that let us ship with confidence. Teams You Might Join

  • Build and evolve the shared services and components that other teams depend on.

The Role

  • Ship features end to end, from planning through production.
  • Partner directly with Product Managers, Designers, and the engineers who build on your work to shape your team's roadmap, not just execute against it.

  • Review code and mentor other developers on your team.
  • Raise the bar on tooling, testing, and delivery practices.

job.name: Staff Fullstack Engineer, Okta Secures AI
job.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Get to know Okta

Okta is The World's Identity Company. We free everyone to safely use any technology, anywhere, on any device or app. Our flexible and neutral products, Okta Platform and Auth0 Platform, provide secure access, authentication, and automation, placing identity at the core of business security and growth.

At Okta, we celebrate a variety of perspectives and experiences. We are not looking for someone who checks every single box. We're looking for lifelong learners and people who can make us better with their unique experiences.

The AI Acceleration Team

AI agents are now acting on behalf of employees, calling tools, reading data, and making changes inside the systems companies care most about. Every one of those actions raises an identity question: who is this agent, who is it acting for, and what is it allowed to do? Okta is building the products that answer it.

The AI Acceleration team exists to get those products to customers faster. We're part of the Okta Secures AI Pillar, and our job is to accelerate its roadmap wherever we can have the biggest impact. In practice, that means picking up high-priority work alongside the teams that own it, ramping quickly, and shipping.

The Staff Full Stack Engineer Opportunity

As a Staff Full Stack Engineer on the AI Acceleration team, your mission is to help build the industry's first Identity Security Fabric for the agentic era. You'll be a technical leader across the Okta Secures AI Pillar's highest-priority work, helping us deliver on our North Star: "To get AI right, you have to get identity right."

You will help deliver our four-pillar maturity model (Discover, Onboard, Protect, and Govern), providing enterprise-grade visibility and governance for both human and non-human identities. By building solutions that move beyond reactive perimeter security, you will help organizations prevent "Shadow AI" and turn AI risk into business value.

This role requires deep expertise in distributed systems and a commitment to AI-native engineering as our standard. You will rethink backend design, validation, and delivery through AI-augmented workflows, ensuring our platform provides secure, interoperable, and scalable access, and enforcing the principle of least privilege for every agent action.

job.name: Staff Design Engineer - Canada
job.description:
Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik, Ashby's Co-Founder and CTO. This role is close to my heart because, as someone who can both design and code, it’s where I’ve always done my best work, but also where I was seen as a rebel and an outsider. I want folks like me to feel at home at Ashby, and so I made Design Engineering a formal role and department that works closely with me. Our first hire was over five years ago, and we’re doubling the team from five to over ten in the next year.

This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. Combining excellence in both is where magic happens. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. For instance, the UX and UI I envisioned often influenced the data model's design and flexibility, while the understanding of technology's capabilities often simplified or improved the design. This role embraces that.

You’ll Work On Our Most Challenging Design Problems, Help Others Improve Their Designs By Expanding And Enhancing Our In-house Design System, And Consult On Bespoke Design Work Needed By Product Engineers. To Ground It With Examples, Design Engineers At Ashby Have:

  • Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

job.name: Member of Technical Staff, Data Platform
job.description:
About Mecka AI Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

The role

A capture is just the beginning. Before that footage becomes a dataset a robotics team can train on, it needs to be uploaded, processed, checked, labeled and packaged. You’ll build the systems that make that happen, along with the tools our operators, researchers and customers rely on every day.

Our Data Platform—internally, the Data Engine—has work for software and machine learning engineers who like understanding how the pieces fit together. You’ll join as a generalist, starting in a pod that matches your strengths and company needs: capture, QA, text labels, delivery or infrastructure and platform. People move between pods as needs change, and you’ll own what you ship.

What you’ll do

  • Build across the stack. You’ll take software from design through production, working across frontend, backend and data systems.
  • Make the tools people need. You’ll build clear, fast interfaces for the operators, researchers and customers using our platform every day.
  • Keep the data moving. You’ll scale the systems that ingest, process, store and serve very large volumes of video and sensor data.
  • Make quality part of the pipeline. You’ll run the systems that check, label and package data, including models working inside those pipelines, and keep bad data from reaching customers.
  • Own how it runs. You’ll take responsibility for reliability, performance and cost, replacing manual work and one-off scripts with durable systems.

What you’ll bring

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals. You bring sound system design and hands-on experience with Python or TypeScript.
  • Experience beyond a single layer. You’ve worked across more than one layer of a production stack, or run models inside production pipelines.
  • Good judgment when systems are live. You’re comfortable monitoring, debugging and fixing production issues.
  • The ability to make sense of ambiguous requirements. You can work with researchers and non-technical users to turn an unclear need into reliable, usable software.
  • Ownership and speed. You scope work tightly, ship a useful first version quickly and follow through on what you build.

Nice to have

Experience in one or more of these areas would be valuable:

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Senior Software Development Engineer in Test — Okta Identity Governance

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

The Okta Identity Governance Team

Okta Identity Governance is Okta's Identity Governance and Administration solution, responsible for some of the most critical and visible workflows in enterprise identity: how people request access, how approvers grant it, how entitlements are enforced, and how organizations prove to auditors that only the right people have the right access.

Okta Identity Governance is the leading contributor to Okta's new product bookings, and it runs inside some of the largest enterprises in the world — the kind of accounts where a single tenant carries hundreds of thousands of identities across thousands of applications.

Quality here is a compliance bar, not just a user experience one. When a governance product has a defect, a company can stay over-provisioned on access it believes it revoked, or hand an auditor evidence that isn't true.

The Senior Software Development Engineer in Test Opportunity

As a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test, you'll own quality for medium-sized features on your scrum team, and co-own larger ones, from the first design review through release and into production. You'll turn the team's test strategy into test plans, write the automation, and hold the release bar for features that have to work at enterprise scale — long-running certification campaigns, tenants with millions of entitlements, dozens of third-party connectors, and audit records that must be provably correct.

You'll work alongside developers as an engineer, not a gatekeeper: reviewing designs and code, building the tools that make coverage cheap, and turning every escaped defect into automation that keeps it from coming back.

job.description:
About Nominal Engineers today are building some of the most ambitious machines humanity has ever seen. They should have AI that’s purpose-built for them.

Nominal is building the Hardware Intelligence Platform that gives engineers increased visibility into complex physical systems, helps them make better decisions, and ultimately gets their products into the real world faster. It brings together the systems, data, intelligence, and applications hardware engineering requires to meet the AI moment. Hardware engineering teams use Nominal to simulate, test, manufacture, and operate the physical systems that keep the world moving, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation energy systems and robotics.

Our customers span aerospace, defense, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and robotics. They include Anduril, Shield AI, Wisk Aero, Pratt Miller Motorsports, Antares, and Shinkei Systems, amongst others, alongside programs within the U.S. Air Force and Navy. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Tesla, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software.

Some of the world’s leading technology investors, including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, and Insight Partners, are backing Nominal’s ambition to change how machines are built and operated. We’re looking for engineers who want to take on hard problems and help make a new generation of world-changing hardware possible.

*Join Nominal as a Frontend Software Engineer, Auth* At Nominal, the frontend goes far beyond a visual layer on top of APIs. For the Auth team, it's where administrators decide who can see and change sensitive test data, and where every user learns what they're allowed to do and why. Our customers run programs where the wrong person seeing the wrong data is a serious problem, so access control has to be precise, and the interface has to make that precision clear.

We're looking for engineers who love reasoning about permission models as much as building intuitive interfaces. You'll work at the intersection of product, design, and engineering to turn a relationship-based authorization system into tools that let admins control access with confidence and let users understand exactly why they can or can't see something. Success in this role is measured by building products that make a precise, deny-by-default permission model legible without hiding its power.
