About The Role Alignerr is building a dataset of expert tasks that train and evaluate advanced AI agents on real enterprise engineering work. As a Task Author based in Bangalore, you will design and calibrate authentic engineering challenges — diagnosing failing integrations from logs, tracing bugs through codebases, and writing and verifying real fixes — that genuinely push the limits of capable AI agents.

Bangalore's engineering talent is world-class, and this role is designed for working engineers with real industry experience in backend systems, SaaS infrastructure, APIs, or enterprise software. This is not a generalist or instructional role — it requires hands-on engineering skill.

  • Organization: Alignerr
  • Type: Hourly Contract
  • Location: Remote
  • Commitment: Flexible, task-based

Key Responsibilities

  • Author realistic engineering task prompts covering integration failures, log-based debugging, bug traces through source code, and configuration or integration fixes
  • Write scoring rubrics that define exactly what a correct fix or diagnosis looks like and how it is verified — including live environment validation where applicable
  • Set up task environments with realistic codebases, logs, alerts, and system states that place an AI agent in a plausible engineering situation
  • Solve each task yourself — write the actual fix and confirm it works — to validate the task is sound and the rubric is accurate
  • Calibrate task difficulty by adjusting code complexity, log volume, failure modes, or ambiguity until the task reliably challenges the model to the intended degree
  • Review and correct AI-drafted task prompts or rubrics when provided

Qualifications

  • Working software engineer with hands-on, industry-level experience — this is not a theoretical or instructional role
  • Fluency in Git, version control workflows, and code review practices
  • Strong debugging skills: comfortable reading logs, using observability tools, and tracing failures through a codebase
  • Experience with infrastructure, integrations, and configuration code (APIs, services, config files, CI/CD)
  • Ability to write and verify a code fix in a live or simulated environment
  • Ability to define precise, checkable correctness criteria for engineering outcomes
  • Strong written communication skills in English

Nice to Have

  • Experience in enterprise SaaS, fintech, or industrial IoT engineering contexts common in Bangalore's tech ecosystem
  • Background with monitoring and observability platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, or PagerDuty
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure on AWS, GCP, or Azure

Job Description: Senior Azure Cloud Consultant

Job Summary

We are seeking a Senior Azure Cloud Consultant to help customers design, build, deploy and improve secure, reliable cloud platforms and solutions on Microsoft Azure.

You will work across the full consulting lifecycle, including discovery, assessment, solution design, implementation, testing, operational readiness and transition to support. You will guide customers through cloud adoption, cost optimization, migration, modernization and platform engineering initiatives, translating business and technical requirements into practical, supportable Azure solutions.

This is a senior individual contributor role combining hands-on engineering expertise with technical leadership. You will influence technical decisions through your expertise and collaborative approach, while taking accountability for delivering successful customer outcomes.

  • Design and improve CI/CD practices using Azure DevOps or equivalent platforms, incorporating source control, automated testing, security scanning, approvals and deployment controls.
  • Design and implement secure Azure solutions aligned with customer security requirements, identity and access management policies, compliance obligations, and Microsoft security best practices.

job.name: Senior Financial Analyst, Commissions
job.description:
As a Senior Financial Analyst, Commissions at Aristocrat, you will play a pivotal role in our success. This outstanding opportunity places you at the core of our operations. You will ensure accurate administration of sales incentive compensation across different business lines and regions. Our company is known for delivering world-class gaming content and innovative tech solutions. Your work will significantly impact both our finance and sales teams. Join us in a setting that supports growth and values your contributions!

What You'll Do

  • Calculate accurate monthly and quarterly sales commissions spanning multiple roles, territories, and lines of business.
  • Interpret incentive plan terms and apply quotas, rates, accelerators, thresholds, adjustments, and other plan provisions consistently.
  • Maintain commission models, participant records, plan documentation, and calculation support with clear audit trails.
  • Support the development, implementation, and ongoing management of sales reward programs, including participant communications and plan changes.
  • Collect, reconcile, and validate source data from sales, finance, and operational systems before calculations are finalized.

job.name: Supply Planner - RTEC; Mars Snacking; Mumbai
job.description:
Job Description Job Purpose/Overview The Supply Planner translates the agreed demand plan into a feasible and executable supply plan that ensures product availability while balancing manufacturing capacity, inventory, service and cost. The role manages supply across multiple planning horizons — the rolling three-month supply plan, the rolling one-month production plan and detailed weekly production requirements — ensuring alignment between market demand and manufacturing capability. In doing so, the Supply Planner serves as the key link between the demand the business wants to fulfil and the supply the organization is capable of delivering.

Job Responsibilities

  • Demand-to-Supply Planning
  • Receive the agreed demand / consensus forecast from Demand Planning and translate it into supply and production requirements by SKU, plant and relevant supply location.
  • Convert unconstrained demand into a realistic constrained supply plan, considering manufacturing capability, inventory, material availability and other supply-chain constraints.
  • Assess changes in demand and determine their impact on production, capacity and inventory.
  • Rolling Supply & Production Planning
  • Develop and maintain the rolling three-month supply plan based on the latest approved demand.
  • Translate the medium-term plan into a detailed rolling one-month production requirement.
  • Convert the monthly plan into weekly production requirements / schedules in coordination with manufacturing teams.
  • Capacity & Constraint Management
  • Evaluate demand against available manufacturing capability and proactively identify supply constraints.
  • Consider line capacity and demonstrated production rates, OEE and utilization assumptions, available shifts and operating hours, planned and unplanned maintenance, changeovers and sequencing, minimum runs / batch sizes, labour availability, quality restrictions, yield and process losses, material availability, shutdowns and external manufacturing limitations.
  • For significant constraints, assess the affected SKU, quantity and period, and determine the impact on product availability.
  • Inventory & Product Availability
  • Ensure appropriate finished-goods availability to support customer demand.
  • Maintain forward visibility of projected inventory and days of cover by SKU / location.
  • Identify potential stock-outs before they occur and initiate preventive actions.
  • Manufacturing & Production Coordination
  • Work closely with manufacturing teams to agree feasible production plans and priorities.
  • Understand plant capacity, operational limitations and production constraints.
  • Validate the feasibility of production plans considering capacity, inventory and availability of required materials.
  • S&OP / IBP & S&OE
  • Provide the consolidated supply view as an input into the S&OP / IBP process.
  • Highlight supply-demand gaps, capacity constraints, inventory concerns and key supply risks.
  • Develop scenarios and recommendations for unresolve

job.name: Credit Analyst - Credit Initiation
job.description:
Job Summary This role exists to support sustainable retail portfolio growth by making prudent, timely and consistent credit decisions for mortgage and wealth management products. The role evaluates customers’ creditworthiness, risk exposure, affordability and application quality to ensure lending decisions align with the Bank’s credit policies, risk appetite, regulatory obligations and business objectives.

The role balances risk management with customer experience by ensuring credit applications are assessed accurately, efficiently and consistently. It contributes to portfolio quality, operational effectiveness and business growth through sound underwriting judgement, risk assessment and continuous process improvement.

The role also supports the evolution of credit operations by identifying opportunities to improve turnaround times, strengthen controls, support product launches and contribute to operational initiatives that enhance service delivery and decision-making effectiveness. Where applicable, the role provides operational guidance, supports team capability development and helps maintain underwriting consistency across the function.

Key Responsibilities Credit Assessment & Underwriting

  • Assess retail mortgage and wealth management applications to deliver prudent credit decisions that balance customer needs with portfolio risk objectives.
  • Evaluate customer financial profiles, affordability, repayment capacity and credit history to determine appropriate lending outcomes.
  • Apply credit policies, underwriting standards and delegated authorities consistently to support high-quality credit decision-making.
  • Escalate complex or higher-risk cases appropriately to ensure sound risk governance and decision integrity.

Credit Risk & Fraud Management

  • Identify, assess and mitigate credit and fraud risks that may affect portfolio quality or customer outcomes.
  • Apply regulatory requirements and internal risk controls to ensure lending decisions remain compliant and defensible.
  • Detect indicators of potential fraud, misrepresentation or suspicious activity and initiate appropriate escalation processes.
  • Support a strong risk culture through disciplined application of credit policies and controls.

Operational Excellence & Process Improvement

  • Improve underwriting efficiency by identifying process enhancements that reduce turnaround times while maintaining control effectiveness.
  • Contribute to operational initiatives that enhance service quality, productivity and customer experience.
  • Support the implementation of new products, policy changes and process enhancements to ensure operational readiness.
  • Use operational insights and performance trends to recommend improvements in credit assessment and workflow management.

Business Support & Stakeholder Collaboration

Role Overview

We are looking for an Application Security Engineer with expertise in both application development and cybersecurity. The candidate should have hands-on experience in VAPT, secure coding, and security assessments of web applications, APIs, and mobile applications. The role also involves direct client communication, coordinating security activities, and ensuring timely remediation of identified vulnerabilities.

Would you like to be the engineer that keeps critical communication and authentication services running across Amazon Dedicated Cloud regions?

Region Services Corporate Infrastructure (RSCI) Collaborative Services is looking for an experienced System Development Engineer with strong Linux, Python, and PowerShell skills to build, automate, and improve services deployed across isolated AWS partitions. You will own the engineering and operational excellence for services including Exchange, Skype for Business, Certificate Authority, Network Policy Service (802.1x/RADIUS), HyperV, Data Protection Manager (DPM), AD user provisioning, artifact delivery via Diode, AI-powered incident notification, and supporting automation, scripting, and monitoring/alarming infrastructure.

This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph. The position further requires the candidate to opt into a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain serverless and containerized systems (Lambda, Elastic Container Service (ECS) Fargate, DynamoDB, Simple Queue Service (SQS), EventBridge) deployed across multiple isolated AWS partitions
  • Write and maintain infrastructure as code (Cloud Development Kit (CDK)/CloudFormation) for multi-region deployments
  • Own CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation across multiple isolated regions
  • Build monitoring, alarming, and observability tooling for service health across air-gapped boundaries
  • Write Python and PowerShell to automate operational processes and integrate systems
  • Participate in design reviews, code reviews, Operational Readiness Review (ORR)s
  • Coach teammates on engineering best practices and operational excellence
  • Provide on-call support

A day in the life

Our mission is to deliver robust, highly available, and easy to use services to our internal customers in support of the Amazon Dedicated Cloud for U.S. Government customers. We are looking for a motivated engineer to deliver results for our customers.

This is a hands-on position where your daily role will design, build, and ship code that improves service reliability, automates manual processes, and delivers new capabilities across air-gapped regions. On a typical day you might troubleshoot a Diode transfer failure blocking artifact delivery to a region, build a new Lambda function to automate a manual AD provisioning step, improve CDK infrastructure for a multi-partition deployment, build automation to improve and develop Windows enterprise services, or investigate why event notifications aren't reaching the right teams.

job.name: Senior Systems Engineer, Virtualization
job.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

What You'll Do HAVOCK builds the software stack that bridges AI workloads and bare metal. We own the operating system, virtualization, runtime, and hardware interfaces that allow thousands of GPU servers to securely execute customer workloads at hyperscale.

This team focuses on the execution layer beneath Kubernetes. We build the systems that provide strong workload isolation, efficient GPU sharing, and high-performance execution across containers and lightweight virtual machines. Our work spans Linux, KVM, container runtimes, GPU drivers, and Kubernetes, ensuring customers can safely run demanding AI workloads on shared infrastructure without sacrificing performance.

About The Role As a Senior Software Engineer on HAVOCK's Runtime & Virtualization team, you'll design and build the execution environment that powers CoreWeave's AI platform. This is fundamentally a Linux systems engineering role where you'll work across the Linux kernel, KVM/QEMU, container runtimes, GPU drivers, and Kubernetes to solve problems that don't have off-the-shelf solutions.

You'll develop secure sandboxed runtimes for GPU workloads, extend virtualization technologies to support new hardware capabilities, optimize the interaction between Linux, hypervisors, and NVIDIA GPUs, and build the tooling that helps engineers understand what's happening across the entire software stack.

The work spans multiple abstraction layers. One day you might be debugging a kernel memory-management issue affecting VFIO device passthrough; the next you might be improving container startup latency, extending KubeVirt to support new GPU workflows, or building eBPF tooling to diagnose production networking and scheduling problems. We value engineers who enjoy understanding how systems behave from the hardware up rather than treating infrastructure as a black box.

Some Of What You'll Work On

Our team builds and operates a serverless deployment platform for enabling AI applications.   • Knowledge of CPU and GPU architecture.

  • Experience in the design, implementation, and release of AI/ML products to market. A flexible technologist familiar with all aspects of the software development lifecycle.

job.description:
About Us

We are the world’s learning company, with over 24,000 employees operating in 70 countries. We combine world-class educational content and assessment, powered by services and technology, to enable more effective teaching and personalized learning at scale. Within Pearson VUE, our Cloud & Platform Engineering team designs, builds, and operates the cloud foundation that powers secure, high-stakes test delivery for millions of candidates worldwide. We believe that wherever learning flourishes, so do people.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Cloud Engineering Manager to lead our Cloud & Platform Engineering team. In this hands-on and managerial role, you will design, build, and operate the enterprise Azure platform and shared services that our product and delivery teams build on — spanning our assessment delivery, exam development, product lines.

You will use Infrastructure as Code, automation, and platform engineering practices to improve the security, consistency, reliability, and developer experience of our cloud estate, which operates under rigorous security and compliance requirements. This role manages a highly technical, engineering-focused team that combines cloud platform development, automation, security and governance, and site reliability with a focus on automation and AI Ops. You will also participate in an on-call rotation supporting business-critical cloud services.

What You’ll Do

Cloud & Platform Engineering

  • Design, build, and operate shared cloud platform services on Microsoft Azure that product teams consume for provisioning, deployment, and day-to-day operations.

Infrastructure as Code & Automation

job.name: Software Engineer (File Storage)-Seattle
job.description:
Our team at Alibaba Cloud builds the core components of the company's storage infrastructure. We provide the foundational cloud technology and services that enable businesses—from merchants and brands to digital content providers—to use the internet to connect with their customers.

We've developed a planetary-scale distributed system that handles hundreds of billions of requests daily and stores multiple exabytes of data. Our focus is on constantly delivering innovative features and solving complex challenges in areas like big data and cloud-native technologies.

We offer reliable, highly scalable, and high-performing distributed file system services that our users depend on for their most critical applications.

  • Contribute to Distributed Systems: Develop solutions for distributed file systems, addressing key challenges in data consistency, fault tolerance, and scalability.
  • Collaborate and Innovate: Partner with product teams to understand requirements and deliver creative technical solutions, while also researching and exploring new storage technologies and architectures.

Job Requirements Minimum Qualifications

We're looking for someone who can hit the ground running. You should have:

  • Deep C/C++ Expertise: You're highly proficient in C/C++ and have a solid grasp of data structures, algorithms, and multi-threaded and network programming.
  • Linux Knowledge: A strong understanding of Linux operating system principles is essential. Experience with kernel development and debugging is a plus.
  • Problem-Solving Skills: You can quickly analyze and solve complex technical challenges.
  • Strong Collaboration Skills: You're a great communicator and can work effectively with a team.
  • Passion for Technology: You have a genuine passion for technology and are excited to tackle new challenges and explore new ideas.
  • Solid Work Ethic: You're honest, diligent, and committed to high-quality work.

job.name: Systems Development Engineer, RSCI Collaborative Services
job.description:
Description Do you have a passion for operating enterprise infrastructure that enables thousands of builders to accomplish their mission in secure, air-gapped environments? Would you like to be the engineer that keeps critical communication and authentication services running across Amazon Dedicated Cloud regions?

Region Services Corporate Infrastructure (RSCI) Collaborative Services is looking for an experienced System Development Engineer with strong Linux, Python, and PowerShell skills to build, automate, and improve services deployed across isolated AWS partitions. You will own the engineering and operational excellence for services including Exchange, Skype for Business, Certificate Authority, Network Policy Service (802.1x/RADIUS), HyperV, Data Protection Manager (DPM), AD user provisioning, artifact delivery via Diode, AI-powered incident notification, and supporting automation, scripting, and monitoring/alarming infrastructure.

This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph. The position further requires the candidate to opt into a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain serverless and containerized systems (Lambda, Elastic Container Service (ECS) Fargate, DynamoDB, Simple Queue Service (SQS), EventBridge) deployed across multiple isolated AWS partitions
  • Write and maintain infrastructure as code (Cloud Development Kit (CDK)/CloudFormation) for multi-region deployments
  • Own CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation across multiple isolated regions
  • Build monitoring, alarming, and observability tooling for service health across air-gapped boundaries
  • Write Python and PowerShell to automate operational processes and integrate systems
  • Participate in design reviews, code reviews, Operational Readiness Review (ORR)s
  • Coach teammates on engineering best practices and operational excellence
  • Provide on-call support

A day in the life

Our mission is to deliver robust, highly available, and easy to use services to our internal customers in support of the Amazon Dedicated Cloud for U.S. Government customers. We are looking for a motivated engineer to deliver results for our customers.

This is a hands-on position where your daily role will design, build, and ship code that improves service reliability, automates manual processes, and delivers new capabilities across air-gapped regions. On a typical day you might troubleshoot a Diode transfer failure blocking artifact delivery to a region, build a new Lambda function to automate a manual AD provisioning step, improve CDK infrastructure for a multi-partition deployment, build automation to improve and develop Windows enterprise services, or investigate why event notifications aren't reaching the right teams.

job.name: Forward Deployed Engineer
job.description:
Exodigo is the leading underground mapping solution for non-intrusive discovery. Our platforms combine multi-sensor fusion, 3D imaging, and AI technologies to create complete, accurate underground maps that enable confident decision-making for customers across the built world. We transform the project lifecycle for our customers, who include key community stakeholders in the utilities, transportation and government sectors.

*We are experiencing sky-rocketing growth and closed a historically large $96M Series B round in July of 2025* .

Job description:

Exodigo engineers the underground without digging. Our platform combines multi-sensor fusion and AI to produce complete, accurate 3D maps of buried utilities, foundations, and geotechnical conditions, which utilities, transportation agencies, and engineering firms use to plan, design, and build with confidence. Behind every map is a team of civil engineers, BIM modelers, and mapping specialists who turn raw subsurface data into engineering-grade deliverables.

We are looking for an AI BIM Engineer to help that team move faster, stay consistent, and scale with our growth. You will work alongside our Mapping, Delivery, and Engineering Services teams, learn how a project moves from field scan through interpretation to Civil 3D and OpenRoads models and client-ready utility maps, and find where AI can take on the repetitive work so our engineers can focus on engineering judgment.

This is a hands-on, builder role. You will scope the problem, build the solution, ship it into live projects, and stay with it until it becomes part of how the team works. You will be the bridge between engineers who know the underground deeply and the AI agents that can amplify them: you can discuss utility quality levels, model QA/QC, and client CAD standards in the morning, and write a new integration for an AI agent in the afternoon. What you learn on our projects will shape the AI capabilities we give every team.

What You'll Do Embed with engineering teams

  • Work side by side with highway, structures, water, and site development teams to understand their design processes, tools, standards, and pain points.
  • Lead discovery sessions with engineers and project leads, and translate what you hear into clearly scoped, prioritized opportunities for AI and automation.
  • Own delivery end to end: from first conversation and rapid prototype through to a stable tool in daily production use.
  • Coach engineers on using AI effectively and safely in their work, through hands-on sessions, office hours, and one-on-one support.

Turn expertise into repeatable workflows

job.description:
About The Role The Forward Deployed Engineer embeds with Hopper's partners, some of the world's largest banks, airlines and travel companies, to bring our AI into their business end to end: getting the data, building and tuning the models, and taking them to production. You will lead data and modelling on site as part of a small forward-deployed team, acting as the bridge between partners and Research. What makes the role distinctive is that the data that matters lives inside partners' own systems, so you make it usable, securely, and turn each deployment into reusable tooling that makes the next partner faster.

What would your day-to-day look like

  • Work on site with partner teams to connect to their systems, including on-premise and legacy platforms, and build secure, reliable data feeds.
  • Map messy, inconsistent commercial data from many sources into one clean model.
  • Build and run pipelines for large historical and near-real-time datasets, with monitoring and data quality checks.
  • Meet partners' security, privacy and IT review requirements, taking only the data the product needs.
  • Design, train and evaluate production ML models for a high-volume commercial use case, choosing the right approach and being clear about the trade-offs.
  • Build the evaluation and measurement that show whether the models are good enough, and where they aren't.
  • Build low-latency, high-throughput services that serve the models in production.
  • Design how the system decides what to answer and how, and how it improves from real usage.
  • Own reliability, cost and performance once the system is live.
  • Partner directly with technology and business teams, from first conversations to go-live.
  • Collaborate with Research and Product, feeding back what you learn in the field.
  • Turn each deployment into reusable tooling so the next partner goes faster.

job.name: Forward Deployed AI Engineer, Travel Intelligence
job.description:
About The Role Hopper powers travel for some of the world’s largest banks, airlines and travel companies, and our Research team builds travel-specialized models. As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer you take that work into a partner’s environment and make it theirs: building the evaluation with their team, preparing their data, training and evaluating the model, and putting it into production where it delivers measurable results. You work in a small forward-deployed team as the person who leads model training on site, across servicing, loyalty, commerce and more, and you are the bridge between our partners and Research.

What Would Your Day-to-day Look Like

  • Work with a partner’s data and business teams to turn their real tasks into a frozen, held-out benchmark across their priority use cases
  • Define what success means for each task, covering task completion, policy adherence, cost and response time, and build the automated graders with human spot checks
  • Establish baselines so results can be compared fairly
  • Prepare training data inside the partner’s environment through extraction, redaction, deduplication, labelling and train/test splits, using only the data the agreed tasks need
  • Run post-training in partnership with Research, applying modern fine-tuning methods to partner use cases
  • Run training on the partner’s cloud and GPUs, or in an environment they approve, under their security and access rules
  • Design experiments that show partners clearly what drives the results
  • Take models from evaluation into production based on evidence, then monitor quality, latency and cost once they are live
  • Use production results to keep improving the model
  • Present results, method and trade-offs to partner data and technology leaders, and defend them
  • Work closely with Research, feeding back what you learn in the field
  • Turn each deployment into reusable tooling so the next partner goes faster
  • Uphold strict data handling, privacy and security standards in every partner environment, and support partner model-risk, security and compliance reviews with clear documentation of data, training and evaluation

job.description:
Position Description

Company Profile:

Founded in 1976, CGI is among the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world.   • Ensure processes for the project is followed for the assessments.

  • Mandatory requirement – Mobile, Web & API Penetration Testing

Technical & Behavioral Competencies

job.description:
Every day, ePayPolicy helps over 10,000 insurance companies speed up incoming and outgoing payments. By helping them move from manual, outdated forms of payment collection to modern payment tools, we help their companies work faster and more efficiently. (Check out our almost 5-star customer reviews.)

How do we do it? With powerful payment tools that just work. Our secure, online ACH and credit card payment page is the core product for many of our companies. But we also provide an integrated suite of helpful features for insurance companies of all sizes, including point-of-sale financing, payables network tools, and check reconciliation, all within a single dashboard.

Our expert, live support team helps deliver exceptional care every day, with an industry-leading 97% customer retention rate. Our customers love us. We love them.

Founded in 2014, our growing team is based in Austin, TX, and has clients in all 50 US states. We’ve grown over 300% in the last three years - with big plans for the future.

The Challenge You'll Own Insurance runs on legacy rails—paper checks, PDF invoices, and fragmented accounting systems. As our Staff Engineer, you will own the architectural blueprint for modernizing this industry through flagship initiatives like Connected AR/AP and Total Recon. These projects eliminate manual invoice entry and automate bank statement reconciliation, saving our customers thousands of hours of manual tracking and false policy cancellations.

Beyond shipping features, you will define how our engineering org builds in the AI era. You’ll bridge our battle-tested C#/.NET core with modern Azure AI infrastructure, establish our spec-driven development standards, and solve real-world latency and indexing bottlenecks at scale. Your architectural judgment will directly dictate how fast and safely we move AI agents into production.

Insurance or fintech background helps, but successful candidates will have a history of proven architectural judgment.

Requirements

  • Must be located in Austin, TX and be available for hybrid work.
  • Proven experience designing and deploying scalable Microsoft enterprise stack solutions with C#, ASP.NET Core, SQL Server, and React.
  • Hands-on track record building production AI systems using Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Search, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures.
  • Deep understanding of AI agent architectures, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and custom indexing strategies to optimize slow agent requests.
  • Familiarity with spec-driven development frameworks like spec-kit or Open Spec.
  • Solid background in Azure cloud architecture, containerization, and Azure cost management.
  • Strong technical leadership skills with experience mentoring engineers, running code reviews, and enforcing high engineering standards.

What You Will Do

job.name: Senior Fullstack Engineer, Finance Technology
job.description:
The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Outreach lets revenue leaders hire AI agents that act rather than advise, working as true teammates that expand capacity and embed the skills of top sellers across every go-to-market workflow, from prospecting and engaging accounts to managing deals, coaching reps, forecasting, and retaining and expanding existing accounts. The Role

The Staff AI Engineer, Full-Stack shapes the product experience of QXO's data and AI platform. This role leads the application architecture and sets the engineering standards that allow teams across QXO to build on the platform, so its judgment influences how multiple teams design, build, and ship.

The role combines product judgment with deep technical ownership: what users see, how the application is structured, and how AI capabilities are presented so people can trust and act on them. job.name: Frontend Software Engineer, Data Platform (Svelte + Rust )
job.description:
At Stoke, we believe a thriving space economy will enable a vibrant, sustainable, and equitable future here on Earth. That is why we’re building Nova, our fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Designed for daily flight, Nova tackles the core challenges of space transportation by reducing cost, increasing availability, and improving reliability. By radically lowering launch costs and increasing flight cadence, we’re helping create a truly scalable space industry.

Our team is mission-driven, collaborative, and empowered to take ownership of their work. If you want to work alongside some of the most dedicated and talented people on Earth, we’d love to have you join us.

Description Reusable launch systems are the key to seamlessly connecting Earth and space. An instrumental ingredient to enabling a rapid launch cadence is the ability to make informed and automated decisions quickly, backed with high quality data. That is our goal for the data team at Stoke, our software empowers our engineers and provides them the ability to automate and improve the efficiency of their day-to-day tasks. As a Software Engineer on the Data Team, you will be responsible for contributing to the design and implementation of Stoke’s data visualization and analysis tooling. Your work will span high-performance web UIs, real-time and batch data services, and scalable systems that monitor the performance and health of supercomputer environments and fielded hardware. You will write production code across the stack, set a high bar for reliability and usability, mentor peers, and help shape a strong technical culture.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain full-stack visualization tools for hardware and software analysis
  • Design intuitive front-end interfaces for troubleshooting, analysis and monitoring the health of our launch vehicles
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to design features that meet real-world, time-sensitive needs
  • Ensure high performance, reliability, and scalability of visualization tools across both front-end and back-end systems
  • Continuously improve existing tools and develop new features to meet evolving requirements
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to a strong technical culture
  • Participate in a low-friction on-call rotation; our platform is stable, but the company depends on what we build

Nice to Have

  • Experience with distributed systems or developer tooling

Why Join Us

  • Work on cutting-edge AI infrastructure alongside leading research labs
  • Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
  • Freelance autonomy with the depth and impact of a senior engineering role
  • Contribute directly to systems that shape how next-generation AI models are built and evaluated

job.name: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Fulfillment Technologies
job.description:
Description Amazon's fulfillment operations run around the clock, and when something goes wrong on the floor, operators need an answer fast. RIVER is the self-service troubleshooting and workflow orchestration platform they turn to first. Starting with AFT operations focus, the platform has expanded much beyond that. If you've worked anywhere near Amazon operations or have used GREF, Concur, Payments etc there's a good chance you've already interacted with our platform.

Over the next years, to keep up with the expanse and scale, we're evolving RIVER from a workflow-centric self-service tool into a standalone, end-to-end, agentic operations product. We're looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build it while it stays live for the operators who depend on it every day.

You will be building a GenAI experience expanding the agentic harness at the core of RIVER and growing it into a complete platform. You'll work across the stack: a natural-language front door that interprets intent from text, voice, or a pasted screenshot; a retrieval layer over a unified knowledge graph (RAG across configurable sources) that generates runnable Skills on demand; an agentic action layer where LLM-driven agents take real actions with guardrails.

Key job responsibilities

  • While our product is heavily focussed on GenAI, you will also get a Full stack developer exposure.
  • You will experiment, design and deliver large scale highly available software.
  • You deliver solutions that scale to our customers using Cloud/AWS Serverless architectures,
  • You monitor the services using suitable metrics and design mechanism for operational excellence.
  • You tackle complex problems, trouble shoot and provide simple and effective solutions.

Basic Qualifications

  • 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
  • 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
  • Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field

Preferred Qualifications

  • 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

job.description:
Description AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

AWS IoT Core enables billions of devices to connect securely to the cloud — and the Identity and Registry team is at the heart of it. We own the foundational primitives that give every IoT device its identity, manage its metadata, and govern how it interacts with the cloud at massive scale.

As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will design and build the systems that customers rely on to provision, authenticate, and manage their IoT fleets — from a single prototype to billions of devices in production. You'll work on challenges spanning distributed systems, security, identity management, and scalable metadata storage and retrieval, directly shaping the experience for some of the world's largest IoT deployments.

This is a high-impact role where your work will be felt across the entire AWS IoT platform and by customers spanning multiple industries — from smart home and automotive to broadcasting and industrial automation. If you're excited about building foundational infrastructure that operates at Internet of Things scale and solving hard problems in device identity and registry, we'd love to hear from you.

Opportunity Overview

We are seeking two engineers to help build the technology foundation for Frictionless Drive Thru, a new capability focused on recognizing customers at the drive-thru order point and connecting that recognition to the correct rewards member and payment experience through NGPOS. The engineering target includes 99.9% recognition accuracy and an architecture capable of operating across thousands to tens of thousands of sensing endpoints.

This is not a traditional application engineering assignment. The work spans IoT, edge computing, proximity and location technology, distributed systems, cloud services, networking, security, and application engineering. job.name: Product Engineer, US
job.description:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs. 🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

job.description:
About Juniper Square Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

Our culture is built for people who want to do ambitious, meaningful work alongside exceptionally talented teammates. We think like owners, move with urgency, and take pride in solving hard problems that truly matter to our customers and the future of private markets. We believe the best ideas come from open debate, deep collaboration, and diverse perspectives, which is why we believe transparency is the default and feedback makes us stronger. If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us!

Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time. About Your Role Juniper Square is the system of record for private-capital funds: we move LP capital, hold investor data our customers are legally responsible for, and enforce the boundaries between one fund’s information and another’s. As a Staff Security Operations Engineer, you will be the senior hands-on engineer who builds our Tier 2 detection and response capability and stands up our data loss prevention program. You will report to the Head of Security and work day to day with the Staff Security Engineer who owns our security platform, the Application Security team, GRC, and the CISO. Our stack is modern and already deployed: Google SecOps for SIEM, CrowdStrike for endpoint, Cloudflare Zero Trust, Upwind for cloud posture and runtime, FireCompass for external attack surface, and a managed detection and response provider we are transitioning away from. The job is to make detection and response something we own, measure, and can prove to auditors and customers.

job.name: Staff Application Security Engineer
job.description:
Your Impact The Staff Application Security Engineer is responsible for securing the design, code, and delivery of applications across the software development lifecycle. Working alongside product and corporate engineering teams, they perform threat modeling, secure design review, code review, and security testing, and drive remediation of the risks they identify.

What You'll Do

  • Secure Development Lifecycle: Embeds security into the software development lifecycle, from requirements and design through build, release, and operation. Partners with engineering teams to define secure coding standards, security acceptance criteria, and release gates that are practical and measurable.
  • Threat Modeling and Secure Design: Leads rapid threat modeling sessions with product and engineering teams to uncover risk early and apply common-sense controls. Produces just-enough design artifacts, and justifies and explains design decisions, including trade-offs and alternative options considered.
  • Application Security Testing: Performs and coordinates application security testing across a wide range of technologies, including manual code review, SAST, DAST, SCA, and secrets scanning. Validates automated findings, records vulnerabilities with clear reproduction steps and recommendations, and works with delivery teams on remediation options. Coordinates third-party penetration tests and drives findings through to closure.
  • Risk Assessment and Remediation: Leads risk mitigation and compensating control efforts that carry potential for high impact on delivery, while containing and minimizing disruption. Understands attack vectors and exploit methods and applies those findings to the DISCO technology stack. Takes multiple data points and stakeholder perspectives into account, and proposes new initiatives, optimizations, and improvements when risks are uncovered during assessments or daily activities.
  • Automation and Tooling: Evaluates, tests, and deploys application security tooling and provides guidance on how best to integrate it into CI/CD pipelines. Writes automation (for example, Python) to reduce manual effort, improve signal quality, and scale vulnerability management coverage.
  • Developer Enablement and Guidance: Answers complex and nuanced application security questions for engineering teams, making judgment calls that involve trade-offs and presenting options with accuracy. Delivers secure coding guidance, training, and reference patterns that raise the security baseline across engineering.
  • Incident Response Support: Participates in the incident response process following the team playbook, contributing application and product expertise to investigation, containment, evidence gathering, and post-incident improvement. Contributes to playbook development and table-top exercises.

2. Strong IAM automation experience across SSO, PAM, provisioning and Joiner/Mover/Leaver lifecycle management

Nice to have

Technical skills

We Are Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.

You Are You have spent years learning that privileged credentials are the keys to the kingdom, and you treat them that way. You know the difference between a secret that is vaulted and one that is sitting in a script somewhere waiting to be found, and you have seen what happens when rotation fails at 3 a.m. on a production database. You do not just manage access, you engineer it with rotation schedules, heartbeat checks, session recordings, and approval workflows that actually hold up under audit.

You are comfortable sitting with an app team to onboard their service accounts into Delinea, writing the PowerShell to automate it, then turning around and explaining to a SOC analyst why a particular Kerberoasting alert fired and what it means. You think in layers: vault architecture, identity governance, machine secrets, and the telemetry that ties it all together. You have operated SailPoint long enough to know that a certification campaign is only as good as the role model behind it, and you have worked with HashiCorp Vault enough to troubleshoot a dynamic secrets engine at two in the morning.

Discovery runs do not scare you, they energize you because finding unmanaged privileged accounts means you get to fix a real problem. At Synopsys, you will operate the identity and privileged access platforms that protect how 30,000 people and thousands of applications authenticate, authorize, and access critical systems every day.

job.name: Senior Security Operations Engineer
job.description:
Overview Team overview

Every cloud depends on a small set of foundational services that almost everything else trusts. Together they form the cloud's Trusted Computing Base (TCB): the services where a small gap can have an outsized blast radius across the cloud and the customers who depend on it.

These are Microsoft's crown jewels, and protecting them is urgent: sophisticated attackers target exactly these kinds of services, and AI is making it faster to find and exploit weaknesses. Securing them is always top of mind for senior leadership, it comes first when we prioritize risk reduction, and the controls we prove here set the paved path for production services across the company.

The TCB Core Security Engineering team in IAM Protect, part of Microsoft's CISO organization, leads this work. We take a data-driven, attack-path view of risk, modeling the trust relationships between services to understand blast radius and focus our effort where it reduces the most risk. We are a technically deep security that operates horizontally across Microsoft. Our strategy is simple to state and hard to do: isolate these services from the rest of the cloud, minimize what has to be trusted, and defend what remains with layered controls.

Role overview

We are looking for a Senior Security Operations Engineer who pairs a deep understanding of how cloud services and platforms are actually constructed with the security instincts to see where they can be broken. You will identify new risks to our crown jewel services, model them with our attack-path and risk data, develop the policies and security controls that close them, and partner with leaders and service owners across Microsoft to drive those controls to adoption until the exposure is measurably gone. Every attack path you shut down is one no attacker can use against Microsoft's cloud or its customers.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

job.name: Lead Software Engineer
job.description:
Job Description

Title: Lead Data Engineer

Location: Any Ipsos Canada Location

Who We Are

Ipsos is one of the world’s largest research companies and currently the only one primarily managed by researchers, ranking as a #1 full-service research organization for four consecutive years. With over 75 different data-driven solutions, and presence in 90 markets, Ipsos brings together research, implementation, methodological, and subject-matter experts from around the world, combining thematic and technical experts to deliver top-quality research and insights. Simply speaking, we help the biggest companies solve some of their biggest problems, serving more than 5000 clients across the globe by providing research, data, and insights on their target markets. And, we’re proud to share we’ve received our Great Place to Work Certification in 2024, for the third year running!

ABOUT The Ipsos DataHub

The Ipsos DataHub is a uniquely positioned group within Ipsos. It is a next-generation data platform designed to unlock the full value of data across the organization. By bringing together information, technology, and expertise in a seamless and secure ecosystem, it empowers teams to move faster, think bigger, and deliver deeper, more meaningful insights. DataHub is at the heart of Ipsos’ vision to transform how data drives decisions, innovation, and impact for clients worldwide.

We’re looking for someone with a deep interest and expertise in data engineering and the dedication to apply that passion. We need someone with the technical expertise to expand and optimize our existing data pipeline and architecture. The ideal candidate will have experience using cloud-based platforms, like Google Cloud Services and AWS, to build and maintain serverless data pipelines to efficiently process and warehouse large scale datasets. The role also requires conscientious attention to detail, an ability to work well on a small team, and a self-starter approach to problem solving and debugging.

What You Can Expect To Be Doing

job.name: Full-Stack Software Engineer III
job.description:
Description & Requirements Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Central Technology is the force multiplier, accelerating creative opportunity and progress at EA. We’re a world-class community of technologists, innovators, strategists, and orchestrators transforming interactive entertainment. Together, we power the platforms, AI-driven tools, live services, and infrastructure that ensure global scale, secure player experiences, and unlock bold new possibilities.

Infrastructure & Platform Services builds and runs the technology foundation for EA’s games. Our teams deliver the live services and backend infrastructure that are used to ship, scale, and operate secure, reliable game experiences for millions of players worldwide.

As a Software Engineer on our team, you will report to the Senior Director of Engineering. You will collaborate with studios to develop internal tools that shape gameplay, progression, and live services. You will maintain an AI-first mentality, finding opportunities to integrate AI and automation into our development lifecycle and product features. You will guide best practices and mentor engineers to provide solutions that support our player-first mission.

Responsibilities

  • You will design components and microservices to ensure our stack supports evolving AI technologies.
  • You will partner with game designers and producers to deliver features in an agile, iterative model.
  • You will perform code reviews and mentor engineers on modern patterns, including the use of AI for tests and documentation.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience building web projects using modern development practices, including frontend UI and backend microservices
  • Hands-on experience building products with AI capabilities, such as prompt engineering, RAG, or agentic workflows
  • Experience building backend services using Node, Kotlin, Go, or similar technologies
  • Experience with TypeScript, including modern patterns such as React hooks, functional components, and advanced type systems
  • Experience deploying services on cloud-based infrastructures such as Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, or Azure

This is a hybrid remote/in-office role.

job.name: Software Development Engineer – Platform
job.description:
Apera is an innovative, Vancouver-based company at the forefront of robotics, AI, and machine vision — recognized with the 2025 Frost & Sullivan Technology Innovation Leadership Award and the 2024 BC Tech "Company of the Year, Growth" award. We're on a mission to redefine AI-driven robotic vision.

Apera AI helps manufacturers make their factories more flexible and productive. Robots enhanced with Apera's software have 4D Vision — the ability to see and grasp objects with human-like capability. Challenging applications such as bin picking, sorting, packaging, and assembly are now open to fast, precise, and reliable automation. We work with the world's leading automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers.

Our portfolio spans Vue (our 4D Vision software), Forge (a no-code simulation and AI training studio where customers build, validate, and de-risk robotic cells before any hardware is bought), and VuePod, our new turnkey, productized bin-picking cell.

Let’s End Robot Blindness. Together. Robots can do amazing things, if they can see.

Apera AI builds breakthrough 4D Vision™ systems that give robots the clarity to handle complex, real-world tasks.

But vision alone isn’t enough, it needs a foundation that scales, updates, and performs flawlessly.

That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Software Development Engineer – Platform to design and build the software foundation that powers Apera’s vision-guided robotics systems.

You’ll solve complex system challenges, bridge hardware and software, and ensure every deployment — from lab to factory floor — runs with precision and reliability.

This is a systems-first role, not app development, not web services.

You’ll design, implement, and maintain deployment frameworks, provisioning tools, and hardware integration layers that make vision-driven robotics scalable and reliable.

What You’ll Actually Do

job.name: Senior Software Developer (.Net)
job.description:
We are seeking a Senior .NET Developer who brings experience in system design and aims to step into an architectural role. Split roughly evenly between hands-on coding and code reviews, your responsibilities will also focus on designing cohesive application structures, data flows, and system integrations.

Your opportunity Our group builds and supports the software that runs the organization's internal operations: custom applications, integrations and data pipelines. As that portfolio grows, we need a senior developer who can deliver hands-on and also help shape our standards and technical direction.

As part of a 12-member team reporting to the Manager, IT Solutions, you will evaluate specifications, construct prototypes, and deliver production-ready code. Over time, the role will expand to include greater architectural responsibility alongside key contributions to core design decisions.

This is a permanent, full-time hybrid role, on-site at least three days a week. Our team is based in London, Ontario, but this position can be based in any of the following Dillon offices: Vancouver, Chatham, Guelph, Hamilton, Kingston, Kitchener, Oakville, Ottawa, Downtown Toronto, North York, Vaughan and Windsor. Responsibilities

  • Software development: Build, maintain and support .NET applications, APIs, integrations and SQL in production.
  • Current-state mapping: In your first 90 days, document our applications, databases, data flows and integrations.
  • Systems integration: Connect on-premise systems with SaaS platforms using REST APIs, scheduled ETL and event-driven patterns where they fit.
  • SaaS data handling: Recommend when to replicate data locally, query it live, or allow read/write, taking licensing, API limits and running costs into account.
  • AI in development: Use AI coding assistants to work faster, and help set team practices for reviewing, testing and securing AI-generated code.
  • AI in our solutions: Identify where AI adds real value in our applications and workflows, and integrate agentic services with attention to data security, accuracy and running cost.
  • Technology recommendations: Evaluate new tools, cloud services and AI, and write clear recommendations covering cost, risk, effort and long-term support.
  • Team mentorship: Support the professional development of junior and intermediate developers through continuous knowledge sharing, collaborative pair programming, rigorous code reviews, and architectural discussions.
  • ERP readiness: Help clean up the data and integration points our upcoming ERP replacement will depend on.
  • Production support: Help investigate complex production issues through to the root cause.

job.name: Sr Software Dev Engineer III, RDS for Oracle
job.description:
Description Amazon Web Services is hiring a Software Development Engineer III for the RDS for Oracle team. We are looking for an experienced engineer to design and build the next generation of managed database services that power mission-critical applications worldwide.

About The Role As a Software Development Engineer III on the RDS for Oracle team, you will own the design and implementation of complex features that scale to millions of database instances. You will work on the full stack—from kernel-level optimizations and storage architecture to customer-facing APIs and operational tooling. Your work directly impacts how enterprises run their most critical databases on AWS.

Key job responsibilities

You will lead the architecture and design of large-scale, distributed database systems using RDS Oracle in AWS cloud environments. This includes optimizing performance for high-availability and scalability, developing solutions that integrate Linux-based RDS Oracle with AWS infrastructure, and designing integrations between Oracle and other AWS services such as EC2, VPC, and IAM.

You will serve as a technical lead for enterprise-level database services, addressing complex customer requirements and concerns. You will collaborate with account managers and solution architects to design and implement database solutions that meet specific enterprise needs. You will engage directly with customers to gather requirements, provide technical consultations, and support complex implementations, translating customer needs into technical specifications and product roadmap items.

You will lead agile development cycles to quickly prototype, develop, and deploy new database features and improvements. You will balance speed of delivery with code quality, security, and scalability requirements. You will stay abreast of competitor offerings and contribute to product strategy by proposing and implementing innovative features to maintain AWS's competitive edge in the database services market.

You will develop and implement strategies for managing database performance at massive scale, supporting thousands of concurrent customers. This includes creating advanced monitoring and troubleshooting tools for large-scale database deployments and designing sophisticated automation systems for database management tasks. You will integrate AI and ML technologies to enhance database performance, security, and ease of use.

You will ensure all database solutions meet required security standards and compliance regulations such as FedRAMP, GDPR, and HIPAA. You will develop and implement security best practices for database management in cloud environments.

job.name: CPU Hardware Verification Software Engineer
job.description:
We are searching for a dedicated Verification/Software Engineer to join the Raven Random Test Generator team at the Arm Austin Design Center. As an engineer on our team, you will help develop and deploy Raven—a powerful dynamic random test generator written in C++ that has been used extensively by CPU design teams throughout the Arm ecosystem for more than a decade. You will collaborate closely with senior CPU verification engineers both inside and outside Arm to understand their verification challenges and develop new ways of achieving their verification goals.

The Raven team is part of Arm’s Architecture & Technology Group, which develops architectural specifications and technologies that enable Arm’s partners to successfully develop processors conforming to the Arm architecture. In addition to supporting CPU verification teams, we collaborate early and frequently with Arm architects to help ensure that new architectural features can be verified effectively.

Your day-to-day work will consist primarily of developing our C++ verification technology and working directly with Raven users and verification teams to solve complex verification problems. This work relies heavily on a strong understanding of computer architecture and the ability to read, understand, and apply new architectural specifications.

If you are looking for a role that combines hardware and software skills, provides opportunities to work on challenging CPU verification problems, and allows you to make meaningful contributions to groundbreaking verification technologies and methodologies, we look forward to hearing from you.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate across the team to develop, document, test, and deploy Raven.
  • Design and implement innovative Raven functionality to enable verification of architectural and microarchitectural features.
  • Design and develop Raven test templates that exercise and stress architectural and microarchitectural features of Arm CPU designs.
  • Investigate, debug, and resolve issues reported by Raven users and internal QA.
  • Work directly with CPU verification engineers to understand verification challenges and develop effective solutions.
  • Use AI responsibly to accelerate engineering work, while leading the resulting changes. Engineers are expected to understand and be able to reason about the code they contribute, and to ensure that all changes are correct, maintainable, and consistent with the team’s software architecture and design philosophy.

job.name: Software Dev Engineer, Amazon Leo Customer Terminal Software

job.description:
Description Have you ever wondered what it takes to build the software systems that turn a rack of AI accelerators from inert silicon into a system a customer can run workloads on? Do you want deep ownership of a service that every one of those systems depends on to boot, run, and stay healthy?

Who are we?

Annapurna Labs is the part of Amazon that designs the custom silicon behind the cloud, including Trainium for AI training, Graviton CPUs, and the AWS Nitro system. Nearly every server in AWS runs hardware we designed. We build the chips, the systems, and the software that power some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world.

What do we do?

We build the software that provisions, operates, updates, and monitors the servers behind AWS's largest AI training workloads, built on Trainium, Graviton, and the AWS Nitro system. We give the people who run this hardware a complete way to stand it up, watch its health, deliver new software to it, and diagnose it, all through open, standard interfaces. We own that software from design through the running system.

Why it's high-impact?

The hardware is just silicon until our software makes it provisionable, observable, and serviceable. Every system runs through what we build. The service you own is on the path for all of them, and the people who run this hardware depend on it every day.

What's the challenge?

There are many ambiguous and difficult challenges in our fast-moving space. Our services require deep system and software expertise. You need to have the ability to work within a fast moving and startup-like environment in a large company. You will identify solutions, trying ideas, given space to fail and iterate to produce products that your customers love.

What you will do?

You own a service in the management plane, in provisioning, monitoring, telemetry, software delivery, or diagnostics, depending on where the team needs you. You take it from design to production, you work backward from what the operator needs, and you build on the interfaces the hardware teams expose.

Who would succeed in this role?

An engineer who likes building and operating a service in production and takes it the whole way. You read logs and reason across process and system boundaries, you ship in small verifiable steps, and you turn requirements into a service other people rely on.

Key job responsibilities

  • Own the design and implementation of a large component or service in the management plane, in provisioning, monitoring, telemetry, software delivery, or diagnostics.
  • Make the application-level trade-offs on your component, and seek direction on the calls that reach beyond it.
  • Automate and simplify the team's development, test, and operations work, and mentor peers as you grow.
  • work backward from customer requirements and deliver solutions that are simple.

Description AWS operates a fleet of servers at the Edge, powering various workloads at cloud scale. We are building the automation, diagnostics, and predictive intelligence that keeps this fleet running at peak. If you want to work at the intersection of hardware, software, and scale — where your code directly prevents customer-impacting failures — this is the role.

We are seeking a Systems Development Engineer to build automation software, diagnostic tooling, and fleet health infrastructure for our compute platforms. You will work across multiple teams and organizations to design scalable, reliable systems for our accelerated compute fleet.

What You Will Do

You will tackle problems no one has fully defined yet — spanning hardware, firmware, kernel, and software simultaneously. You will own systems end to end, writing code that prevents failures rather than reacts to them, and building automation that replaces manual toil with intelligent self-healing. You will work across PCIe topology, Networking, and critical subsystem diagnostics, Linux drivers, and telemetry pipelines to correlate signals and isolate faults at fleet scale.

Why You Will Love It

Your automation runs at a large scale across servers in the cloud. When you ship, you see failure rates move within days. The team is small enough that your decisions shape the architecture, and large enough that you will always have experts to learn from across hardware, firmware, and software.

The Ideal Candidate

You know the full stack from bare-metal to userland. You debug at the intersection of components, not just within them. You build at cloud scale and care how your systems decisions impact customers. You are an excellent communicator who can drive alignment across hardware, software, and operations teams.

Key job responsibilities

Fleet Health & Predictive Infrastructure

  • Build and own the automation infrastructure for fleet health at a large scale of servers, driving toward zero-touch operations that detect, diagnose, triage, and remediate faults without human intervention
  • Design and develop test frameworks, test coverage strategies, and diagnostic tooling to validate hardware functionality, detect faults, and ensure qualification coverage across the platform lifecycle.
  • Design predictive failure detection using telemetry, sensor data, error trending, and log correlation to identify degrading components before customer impact
  • Develop monitoring dashboards and alerting for real-time fleet health visibility across manufacturing, lab, and production environments
  • Define and track fleet health metrics: failure rates, mean time to detect and resolve issues, first-time fix rate, test dwell time, and predictive accuracy

Debugging & Troubleshooting

job.name: Embedded Engineering Intern
job.description:
Come Join Our Team

TASI Measurement takes pride in building quality measurement products and enriching the lives of the people who make them possible. Our interns contribute to meaningful work, learn from experienced engineers, and gain practical experience in a supportive, hands-on environment. This role is designed as a structured learning experience and a potential talent pipeline for future engineering openings.

Who We Are

Seametrics is a designer and manufacturer of a variety of flow metering and submersible sensor products. Since 1990, we have provided innovative solutions to users in irrigation, water & wastewater, environmental, and processing applications. Our focus on innovation, product value and customer accessibility has resulted in over two decades of continuous growth. Seametrics is dedicated to helping conserve the world’s most valuable resource by providing our customers with precision flow meter and environmental sensor products. Being part of TASI Measurement provides the resources of a larger organization with a decentralized operating structure that keeps teams close to customers and their needs. The Engineering team develops and supports electronic measurement products, embedded firmware, test methods, and the documentation required to move products from concept through production and service.

What We Offer

  • Hands-on experience supporting embedded product development and engineering improvement work.
  • Mentorship, feedback, and regular one-on-one guidance from experienced engineers.
  • Exposure to microcontrollers, firmware, electronics test, laboratory tools, and controlled engineering processes.
  • Opportunities to collaborate across firmware, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, quality, and service teams.
  • Opportunities to present work, document results, and build a portfolio of practical engineering experience.

Job Summary The Embedded Engineering Intern will support the Engineering team with supervised work involving embedded firmware, electronics bring-up, test and troubleshooting, data collection, and technical documentation. The intern will work on a defined project with measurable learning objectives and will build practical experience in the tools, methods, and design controls used to develop and support measurement products. By the end of the term, the intern should be able to explain the problem addressed, the engineering work completed, the evidence collected, and the recommended next steps.

Projects

We're looking for Senior C++ Engineers to build, optimize, and scale the data pipelines, annotation tooling, and evaluation systems that leading AI labs depend on to train and improve frontier models.
